title: PCB-Routed Font Renderer
text: A monoline font system (font.js/hanzi.js) that draws text using 0/45/90-degree traces with chamfered corners and round caps, mimicking PCB silkscreen.
how: Implement a canvas-based text renderer that uses the provided glyph stroke data to draw text as vector traces, replacing standard web fonts for our 'lab look' titles.

title: Nested Coordinate Level Renderer
text: A hierarchical rendering system (levels.js) that handles infinite zoom/dive transitions by nesting coordinate systems, allowing cameras to move between parent and child boards seamlessly.
how: Integrate the 'toChild' and 'toParent' matrix transformation logic into our HyperFrames pipeline to enable smooth, mathematically precise 'dive from orbit' transitions.

title: Octilinear Routing Engine
text: A geometry utility (geo.js) that forces lines to 45-degree angles (octilinear), essential for creating authentic-looking circuit board traces and technical UI diagrams.
how: Add the 'octi' function to our geometry library to automatically snap UI connection lines and flow charts to 45-degree increments.

title: Octilinear Diagram Routing
text: Using an 'octi' function to constrain paths to 45-degree and 90-degree angles (PCB style). This creates a clean, technical 'lab' look for connecting nodes or drawing geographic features like rivers as copper traces.
how: Update `compose_lab.py` to include an `octilinear_route` helper for flows and UI panels, ensuring all connecting lines snap to 45/90 degree increments for a sharper aesthetic.

title: Geographic-to-PCB Coordinate Mapping
text: Mapping real-world longitude/latitude coordinates to a local PCB coordinate system (1 unit = 1 km) with scaling factors. Allows placing 'cities' as pads and 'rivers' as traces while maintaining spatial accuracy.
how: Apply this in `compose_lab.py` for tech explainers involving maps. Use the `P(lon, lat)` conversion logic to draw accurate but stylized data-viz maps.

title: Procedural Film-Look LUTs
text: Instead of static LUT files, the system generates color grading curves procedurally using numpy (exponential decay for shadows/highlights and specific RGB channel clipping), ensuring consistent 'film' aesthetics across all assets.
how: Replace our current static color correction with a `grade.py` module that uses the provided `make_luts` logic to apply a consistent dark-metallic/sodium-orange look.

title: Hand-Lettering Skeleton Data
text: The `glyphs.json` file maps characters to coordinate skeletons (paths), allowing for procedural handwriting animations that are more authentic than standard font-based 'write-on' effects.
how: Use this data structure to animate our kinetic titles, drawing lines along the skeleton coordinates rather than just masking a font.

title: Reveal-Time Shader Masking
text: Define a 'reveal time' (arev) attribute for every vertex in a mesh. Use a fragment shader to discard pixels where the current time is less than the reveal time, creating a procedural 'draw-in' effect across complex 3D objects.
how: Implement this in our Three.js lab-look renderer to animate the appearance of 3D props (chips, circuit boards) as if they are being sketched in real-time.

title: Automated Puppet Extraction
text: The extract.py tool uses green-screen keying and scipy.ndimage to automatically segment character sheets into individual, pivot-ready parts with consistent margins.
how: Add this to our pipeline to process character sheets generated by FLUX/Muse, automatically creating the parts/ folder and index.json needed for our animation engine.

title: Automated Asset Provenance Tracker
text: A centralized footage manager (footage.py) that fetches assets from archives (NASA, Commons), stores them with metadata (license, source URL, credit), and generates a SOURCES.md file.
how: Add a metadata-tracking layer to our footage-fetching scripts to ensure every asset used is logged with its license and source for compliance.

title: Event-Driven Layout Orchestrator
text: A central events.json file that drives layout changes, HUD updates, and camera swaps, decoupling the visual logic from the rendering loop.
how: Refactor compose.py to ingest an event timeline rather than hard-coding scene transitions, allowing for dynamic multi-cell split-screen layouts.

title: Parametric Character Rigging
text: A system for defining characters (girl, lamb, moon) as fully parametric objects with view, expression, and pose states, allowing for procedural animation without complex skeletal rigs.
how: Adopt this state-based approach for our recurring characters in 'Puraan Ki Katha' to simplify animation logic and ensure visual consistency across different poses.

title: Book-Pullback Transition
text: A technique for transitioning from a full-screen scene into a 3D-simulated book page, including perspective-corrected page turning and gutter shadow rendering.
how: Use the perspective-mapping logic from end.js to create a 'story-book' transition for our 'Puraan Ki Katha' series, pulling out from the story into a book view.

title: Wax-Resist Watercolour Simulation
text: Simulate watercolour washes by using a wax-coverage map to resist pigment, creating tide lines at edges and granulation in deep paper pits.
how: Update our lab look to include a wash-pass shader that uses a coverage map to modulate pigment transmission based on paper-grain depth.

title: Grouped Layer NPR Rendering
text: Organize scene objects into depth layers (bg, ch, fg) with distinct crayon rendering styles per layer. Apply randomized stroke parameters (angle, gap, width) with controlled opacity. Use silhouette extraction and variable outlines to create depth.
how: Extend compose_lab.py to support layer-based grouping. Apply NPR shaders to layers with unique color palettes and stroke patterns for foreground emphasis.

title: Gradual Revelation Technique
text: Hide key story elements until climax, revealed through character perspective. Clues integrate subtly without explicit pauses - passed visually via background props that guide attention.
how: In storyboarding, plan a final reveal shot (e.g., deity's face through character's eyes for mythology videos). Background props (ancient artifacts, tech gadgets) as visual cues.

title: Dynamic Environmental Simulation
text: Add subtle wind effects using sine waves + noise for organic movement. Parameters: amplitude varies per element (0.03 for flowers, 0.09 for wild grass), frequency at 1.1-2.3Hz. Creates continuous life.
how: Implement GSAP wind effects in HyperFrames for trees, banners, or fabric elements. Apply sine waves with randomized offsets using JavaScript Math.sin().

title: Light-Sweep Reveal Canvas Shader Pass
text: Simulate a premium tech keynote light sweep using an offscreen canvas mask. Calculate length L along sweep angle normal: front = -soft + p * (L + soft * 2). Clip source via linear gradient mask with destination-in, and render a leading-edge highlight band (width band * 2) using 'lighter' composite mode at alpha 0.2-0.55 over the revealed pixels.
how: Implement in HyperFrames compose_lab.py to animate stat cards, tech feature unveils, or product shots upon voice hook triggers.

title: Per-Glyph Rolling Digit Scramble
text: Render high-energy kinetic numbers by giving each digit a staggered lock timestamp. Before lock time lk, substitute the digit with random characters sampled from '0123456789#%/*+=<>?$&@ABCDEFXZ' at 24fps with 3-tap vertical ghosting alpha [0.85, 0.3, 0.14]. At lk, snap into the true digit with a damped spring vertical bounce: dy = -px * 0.12 * exp(-d * 14) * cos(d * 40).
how: Add to compose_lab.py for stat counters and metric reveals in tech explainer reels.

title: Greedy Nearest-Slot Tile Flight Transition
text: Transition scattered elements into an organized grid by calculating Euclidean distances from all active items to target slots. Assign greedily using a sorted distance matrix. Animate each item along a curved quadratic Bezier arc with back(p, 1.35) elastic overshoot and rotational spring damping, morphing asset geometry into standardized grid tiles across 0.35s.
how: Implement in compose_lab.py for multi-asset summary cards, comparisons, and grid assemblies.

title: The 'Verdict' UI Plate
text: A specific UI pattern for summary facts: a rounded rectangle plate (#efebe4) at 84% opacity with a 2px accent line that grows via eo() easing. Text is 46px Noto Sans SC in the accent color.
how: Implement as a new layout component in `compose_lab.py` for the final summary scene of tech explainers.

title: Stack-Top Readout Pinning
text: Pin data labels to the 3D coordinate of the top-most item in a stack. The leader line runs from the stack top to a 2D overlay plate that remains in a 'safe zone' (80px from edges).
how: In the Three.js pipeline, project the 3D coordinate of the last element in a list to 2D space and draw the leader line in the overlay canvas.

title: Hero Asset Impact Logic
text: For the final 'hero' asset landing, layer a low-frequency punch (70-105Hz sine sweep) + bass drum + timpani + metal ring resonance. Follow the main hit with 5 micro-bounces (diminishing volume) to simulate weight.
how: In `mix.py`, trigger a composite 'Impact' function at the final timestamp, including the micro-bounce sequence.

title: Automated Cue-Sync Auditor
text: Verify that every visual 'spawn' event (file appearance, notification) lands exactly on a musical note or beat. Use a bisecting search to find the nearest audio note timestamp; flag any visual event more than 6ms off-sync.
how: Create `audit_sync.py` called by `preflight.py`. Compare the `events.json` (visuals) against the `score.json` (audio) generated by the music engine.

title: Squash and Stretch Physics
text: Use procedural envelope functions (sinusoidal squash/stretch) for object landings and pops. A 'pop' technique (sticker-to-3D-object) adds significant polish to UI elements.
how: Integrate anim.js squash() and pop() functions into our GSAP render loop to make UI panels feel 'alive' when they appear.

title: Ducking Envelope System
text: Use uniform_filter1d on voice-over activity to create a smooth, automated ducking envelope for background music, preventing harsh volume jumps.
how: Replace manual volume automation in mix.py with a calculated ducking envelope based on the voice-over's active timestamps.

title: Sub-frame Accumulation for Motion Blur
text: Instead of standard post-process blur, render N sub-frames per output frame, jittering camera position and time, then average them. This provides physically accurate motion blur and depth-of-field without expensive GPU blur shaders.
how: Implement an AccumPass in our HyperFrames renderer that loops N times per frame, jittering the camera matrix and time variable before compositing.

title: Automated Font Subsetting
text: Reduce font file sizes by subsetting only the characters actually used in the script and UI, significantly improving render times and web-load performance.
how: Create a font_subset.py tool using fontTools that reads our script files and exports a minimal .ttf file for the render pipeline.

title: Procedural Engraving Engine
text: Integrate the `burin.js` engine to generate high-quality, 'hand-drawn' cross-hatching and contour lines for diagrams and props. This uses distance fields to automatically model tone and form.
how: Port `burin.js` to a Python-compatible format or use a Node.js sidecar to generate SVG/Canvas assets for the 'lab look' UI panels and 'Puraan Ki Katha' illustrations.

title: Procedural Fur and Stipple
text: Use the `fur` and `stipple` algorithms to generate organic, non-repetitive textures for mythology-themed videos. These functions use density and tone functions to place elements naturally within shapes.
how: Add these functions to the `compose_lab.py` or a new `assets.py` to procedurally texture characters or props in 'Puraan Ki Katha' stories.

title: Particle-Pool Continuity
text: Maintain visual continuity by using a fixed pool of particles that 'become' different objects across acts through staggered blending. This creates a seamless, fluid transition style that feels more sophisticated than standard cuts.
how: Implement a 'particle-pool' class in our visual engine that tracks a set of points across scenes, allowing them to morph between different UI layouts or props.

title: Deterministic Frame Engine
text: Design the render pipeline so that any frame 't' can be computed independently of the previous frame. This eliminates state-dependent render failures and allows for massive parallelization and instant recovery of stuck jobs.
how: Refactor preflight.py and compose.py to accept a single timestamp 't' and return a complete state object, removing global state dependencies.

title: Two-Tone Shading System
text: The flat.js implementation uses a 'shaded' helper to create depth by layering a base color and a shade color with a fixed pixel offset. This creates a clean, premium 'flat-space' look without expensive shaders or gradients.
how: Implement the 'shaded' and 'twoTone' functions in our compose_lab.py to add depth to UI panels and character props automatically.

title: Sight-Line and Next-Stop Logic
text: The sightGeom and nextRing functions calculate dynamic paths between objects (e.g., Orbi to a galaxy) and render dotted lines that stop short of the destination, providing clear visual cues for explainers.
how: Add a module to our pipeline that calculates the vector between the current hero asset and a target coordinate to draw these 'sight lines' during transitions.

title: Character Expression Sheet
text: A structured way to define character states (front, side, happy, zoom) as a function of expression and view, ensuring consistency across scenes.
how: Adopt the 'sheet.js' approach for our recurring characters: define a JSON 'rig' that maps expressions to specific asset transforms.

title: Perspective Camera Rig
text: A 2D-to-3D projection camera system that simulates tilt, heading, and FOV for flat assets, creating a '3D-on-a-plane' look without full 3D rendering.
how: Port the camera.js projection logic to our GSAP/HyperFrames pipeline to allow for 'dolly' and 'tilt' effects on our static lab-look assets.

title: Volume-Preserving Eased Spring Squash
text: Standard overshoot entrance curves (like back.out) scale both width and height simultaneously, causing an unnatural ballooning effect. Retain visual mass during spring-ins by coupling the back ease with an orthogonal squash factor: sc = E.back(p), sq = 1 + 0.25 * Math.sin(p * Math.PI) * (1 - p), setting scaleX to sc / sq and scaleY to sc * sq along travel direction.
how: In compose_lab.py, update kinetic typography and pop-in badge transforms to divide horizontal scale and multiply vertical scale by sq during entrance.

title: Layered Reveal Technique
text: Complex assets (like the avocado chair or castle) are broken into multiple SVG layers (L[0], L[1], L[2]) that are revealed sequentially based on the beat, creating a sense of 'construction' or 'assembly' rather than a static pop-in.
how: Update our `compose_lab.py` to support multi-layer asset definitions that accept a reveal-index, allowing us to animate complex diagrams appearing in stages.

title: Modular 'Bean' Character System
text: The system uses a single 'bean' function with modular parameters (color, belly, antenna, accessories) to represent different AI models consistently. Characters share a common skeletal structure (arms, eyes, mouth) while using specific visual markers (e.g., 'lens' for DeepSeek, 'beret' for Mistral) to differentiate them.
how: Implement a 'CharacterFactory' in our HyperFrames pipeline to generate consistent avatars for recurring AI models, ensuring they look identical across different videos.

title: Procedural UI/Prop Factory
text: The source demonstrates creating complex UI elements (podiums, banners, cards) using simple SVG primitives and coordinate-based layout logic. It uses a 'bannerAnim' and 'card' system that handles text measurement and layout scaling automatically.
how: Create a library of reusable SVG UI components (e.g., 'Verdict' plates, 'Stat' counters) that auto-scale based on text length, replacing static image-based assets.

title: Fixed-offset voice alignment
text: Trim TTS leading silence so first audible sample starts at fixed 25 ms. Then schedule voice 20–30 ms before target beat — it lands exactly on beat. Removes variable latency from TTS engines.
how: In voice gate (after TTS), measure onset (first sample >1% peak). Trim to (onset - 15 ms) then pad 10 ms silence → 25 ms fixed start. Adjust plan.py timing to place voice at beat - 0.025 s.

title: Style config JSON
text: Per-page style metadata (slug, en/cn names, film title, line, uses, frame_sec, dur, BPM, palette) in JSON. Centralizes theming for planner, composer, thumbnail, and analytics.
how: Create styles/{kaise-tech,puraan-katha,aage-suno}/style.json. Load in ideas.py, plan.py, compose.py, thumb.py. Use BPM for beat helpers, palette for colors, dur for pacing checks.

title: Parallel segment rendering
text: Split timeline into N equal segments (default 6). Render each in parallel via headless Chrome (Playwright) piping PNG frames to ffmpeg. Supports partial re-render via SEGS env var (e.g., only last segment after fix).
how: Modify render pipeline (HyperFrames) to accept --segment-start --segment-duration. Launch N workers via subprocess/asyncio. Concatenate with ffmpeg concat demuxer. Add SEGS env to doctor.py for targeted re-renders.

title: Animated banner component
text: banner(year, name, sub, color) creates a styled card; bannerAnim(b, t, t0, t1) handles elastic entrance/exit with overshoot. Consistent timeline/title cards across videos.
how: Add banner() and bannerAnim() to compose_lab.py as GSAP timelines. Use in plan.py for 'era' transitions (e.g., 2017 Transformer, 2022 ChatGPT). Parameterize colors from page palette.

title: Event-driven SRT generation
text: From events.json (v:* events) generate SRT, merging duplicate cues within 150 ms. Handles multi-voice shouts (hey_a, hey_b…) and robot FX. Adapts to Hinglish/Devanagari.
how: Write make_srt.py reading events.json + voices/shouts.json (map to our voice IDs). In publish.py, run after audio render to produce .srt for Instagram/YouTube. Add Devanagari transliteration step.

title: Per-Pixel Material Lighting Mask (Glint Pass)
text: Light only affects pixels where a 'material mask' (gold leaf) is non-zero. Each mask texel stores surface tilt (normal). Lighting shader computes N·L per pixel, multiplies by mask, adds Fresnel-like cup factor. Non-mask areas (ink, vellum) stay matte.
how: In compose_lab.py (Canvas/WebGL), render 'lab materials' (PCB traces, chip dies, hologram edges) to an offscreen mask texture with encoded normals (R=tiltX, G=tiltY). In composite pass, sample mask; if alpha>0, apply lighting (radial/band/ring lights from scene) using tilt. Gives 'physical' feel to 2D UI.

title: Time-Warp Aware Hook Placement
text: Hook visual (Frame 0) and audio (first word) are placed on *film clock* 0.0. Story clock may start earlier (e.g., -0.5s pre-roll). The warp map ensures the 'core shock fact' lands at film 0.0 even after compression. Subtitle SUBS timestamps are film-clock.
how: In plan.py, when scoring hooks, simulate the warp map: ensure hook trigger (visual + audio) maps to film_t ≤ 0.5s. Adjust story_t accordingly. Validate in preflight.py by checking events.json for 'vo' at film_t ≈ 0.6s.

title: Single-Command Reproducible Build (build.sh pattern)
text: One shell script orchestrates: font fetch → TTS (+ASR) → events export → audio mix → SRT gen → video render (workers) → mux (loudnorm -14 LUFS) → readcheck → poster/styleframe extraction. Env vars for LIB, PY, WORKERS, VOICE=1 re-record.
how: Consolidate studio's scattered scripts (ideas.py, research.py, plan.py, compose.py, mix.py, publish.py) into a single build.sh entry point per page. Use make or just for dependency tracking. Adds 'doctor.py' self-repair as a build target.

title: Shot-independent staging for product/fable shorts
text: main.js poses camera, product, and lights independently per shot (dark, open, macroA, macroB, explode, front, channels, pair, caustics, reveal). No spatial continuity needed; each shot optimizes its own composition. Reduces rigging complexity and allows dramatic angle jumps.
how: In plan.py, enforce 'shot independence' rule: each scene gets its own camera/lighting preset; no cross-shot position constraints. Use for Kaise Tech product explainers and Puraan Ki Katha mythic close-ups.

title: Gold-leaf illumination rendering technique
text: Layered drawing: 1) flat pigment fill, 2) inner darker rim (rimShade), 3) ink line, 4) gold leaf (leaf/leafCord) with burnish highlight, 5) punched/dimpled texture (punch rings), 6) pearl lines. Colors: vermilion bole base, gold leaf, ink outlines. Simulates medieval manuscript illumination.
how: Create a new 'gilded' variant in compose_lab.py: replace lab's mono HUD palette with bole/gold/ink. Use GSAP to animate leaf application (stroke-dashoffset) and burnish flash. Target for Kaise Tech 'heritage tech' specials or Puraan Ki Katha title cards.

title: Beat-synced visual sweeps locked to audio kicks
text: In main.js, light sweeps (diagonal highlight bands) trigger exactly on kick drums (KICKS array). Macro shots (macroA/macroB) fire a 0.45s sweep per beat via MACRO_SWEEPS timestamps. Sweep azimuth matches camera for correct reflection.
how: In compose_lab.py, add a beat-sweep component: read beats from music/score.json (kicks_808), create GSAP timeline with sweep overlays (diagonal gradient) at each beat, sync azimuth to camera rotation. Use 120/200 BPM Rhythmic Grid from brain.

title: Shot list timeline structure
text: story.js SHOTS = [[start_bar, end_bar, shot_name], ...]; shotAt(t) returns current shot. Cuts only on bar boundaries. VO and SFX timestamps reference absolute seconds.
how: Adopt in plan.py: output scenes with bar-aligned start/end; add shot_name to scene metadata; use in preflight.py to verify cut alignment.

title: Font subsetting with unicode-range change detection
text: fetch_fonts.mjs downloads Google Fonts WOFF2 slices, rewrites fonts.css only when unicode-range coverage changes (byte-for-byte compare after normalizing line endings). Caches slices in fonts/; git stays clean on rebuild.
how: Integrate into tools/fetch_fonts.py: after downloading slices, compute range coverage; only overwrite fonts.css if ranges differ; commit fonts/ and fonts.css together.

title: Light-guide pulse shader
text: guideMat in product.js: MeshPhysicalMaterial with onBeforeCompile injecting a fragment shader that draws up to 8 comet-shaped pulses along UV.x (Gaussian head + exponential tail). wrap=true makes a ring. Pulses driven by uniform array uP[8] (pos, width, intensity, hue-mix).
how: Port to Three.js in compose_lab.py as LightGuideMaterial; bind pulse data from audio beats (KICKS) or data viz; use for cable flows, neural paths, UI scan lines.

title: Dark-field caustic floor shader
text: studio.js floorShader: Reflector with custom fragment shader doing 12-tap blurred reflection, Voronoi caustics with per-channel dispersion (RGB scale offsets), sound-wave rings (band-pass colored), and seamless background melt. Uniforms: uC[3] caustic sources, uWave[12] rings, uTime.
how: Port to HyperFrames as a WebGL layer under Three.js scenes; feed uC from product glass positions, uWave from audio beats; renders at 1920×1080 with 4× MSAA.

title: Section plane sweep for cutaway diagrams
text: main.js animates a clipping plane (sweepClip) that moves across the 3D phone model, revealing internal layers (battery, board, coil) in sync with narration. The plane edge is rendered as a dashed line with a 'SECTION' label. This visual grammar — sweep → reveal → label — is directly transferable to 2D HyperFrames for 'inside the device' explainers.
how: In compose_lab.py, implement a 'section sweep' component: a vertical/horizontal line that wipes across a composite image (or layered divs), revealing a second layer underneath (e.g., PCB inside phone). Sync to narration keyword ('inside', 'under the hood'). Add a dashed line overlay and 'SECTION' label using the existing card/label system.

title: Automated clean poster & style-frame capture
text: poster.mjs launches the render page with ?subs=0 (no subtitles), seeks to a predefined timestamp (e.g., 17.4 s), and saves a high-quality JPEG for the poster and a gallery style frame. This guarantees the poster matches the final render exactly, without manual scrubbing.
how: Add a poster capture step to build.sh: after mux, run a headless capture (Playwright) at the designated 'poster time' (stored in style.json) with subtitles disabled. Save as poster.jpg and stills/styleframe.jpg. Use the same viewport and render settings as the video.

title: Procedural pixel character atlas with parameterized poses
text: Characters are drawn pixel-by-pixel into a texture atlas; each frame is generated by a function taking parameters (walk phase, arm state, lantern intensity, kneel, blink, look direction). This yields 30+ distinct frames per character from ~200 lines of deterministic drawing code.
how: Replace manual sprite sheets for recurring characters (e.g., Wren, Keeper) with a Python/Canvas script that emits atlas PNGs + JSON frame metadata. Use in compose_lab.py for 'inanimate prop expressive acting states'.

title: Dynamic character-attached point light with shadow
text: Wren's lantern is a THREE.PointLight parented to her hand (position derived from atlas frame coordinates). It casts shadows (1024² map), has a glow sprite, and its intensity flickers via flick(t, seed). The light drives scene illumination and bloom.
how: In compose_lab.py, when a 'lantern' prop is present, add a dynamic point light in the HyperFrames 3D layer (if using Three.js via headless) or simulate with a radial gradient overlay that tracks the prop's screen position.

title: Deterministic particle systems for rain, fireflies, dust, sparks
text: Particles are CPU-simulated Points: positions computed from time t using seeded hash (h2) and sine waves. Each system (rain, fireflies, dust, embers) has ~100 particles, updated every frame via a userData.update(t) callback. No GPU simulation needed.
how: Port to Python/NumPy for offline render: generate particle position CSVs per shot, then drive HTML/Canvas particles in HyperFrames. Use for 'storm' and 'lamp room' atmospherics in Kaise Tech/Puraan Ki Katha.

title: Procedural Pixel-Art Texture Generator
text: Deterministic functions for wood planks, cobbles, rock strata, half-timber plaster, shingles, and dirt/grass ground (px.js). Uses Bayer dither, fBm noise, Worley cells, and luminance ramps. Outputs a canvas texture at any resolution, seedable per shot.
how: Port `woodPlanks`, `cobbles`, `rock`, `plaster`, `shingles`, `ground` to a Python `textures.py` using Pillow/NumPy; call from `compose_lab.py` to generate unique background plates for 'lab look' scenes without Muse/FLUX calls.

title: Procedural Music Synthesis for Custom Beds
text: Synthesize a 120 BPM orchestral-style score entirely in NumPy (score.py, not shown but referenced): generate harmonic pads, bass lines, percussion, and crescendos from code. Output stems (score.wav + score.json with hit points) for precise alignment. Zero licensing, infinite variations.
how: Create `music/synth_score.py` using `librosa`/`scipy` for oscillators, envelopes, and mixing. Drive from `plan.py` mood tags (tension, relief, climax). Replace stock music beds for 'lab look' and 'classic' pages. Keeps stack free.

title: Target box lock animation (tilt→straight, scale→fit, flash)
text: Box starts large, rotated 45°, scales down and straightens over ~0.5 s using ease-out-cubic; on lock frame a white flash (3 px) and label appear. Lock progress drives label fade-in after 80% complete.
how: Implement targetBox() in compose_lab.py for 'clues' callouts. Trigger from plan.py scene beats; use eo(k) easing. Flash frame emits 'lock' audio event for mix.py.

title: Coarse-to-Fine Stroke Placement (Hertzmann)
text: Strokes placed in passes of decreasing radius (36→18→9→4.5→2.5px). Each pass only adds strokes where current render error > threshold (per shape-group). Big knives lay color planes; tiny dabs fix edges. Guarantees detail where needed, economy elsewhere.
how: When generating procedural 'lab look' elements (charts, diagrams), use multi-pass placement: coarse grid for backgrounds, finer for axes, finest for labels/data points. Drive by pixel-error against a reference raster.

title: Height-Field Lit 2.5D Panels
text: The impasto renderer writes stroke height/coverage to a 16-bit float texture, then lights it in a second pass (raking light, wet specular, canvas weave where paint is thin). Gives flat panels physical depth and materiality.
how: Add a WebGL2 fragment shader pass in HyperFrames (or use Canvas2D filter chain) that reads a 'height' layer from lab-look panels (stat bars, UI cards) and applies lighting with uNorm, uSpec, uWeave uniforms. Toggle per style config.

title: Procedural Crowd Choreography on Beat Grid
text: Nine walkers/umbrella holders assigned fixed positions, pop times (POPS[]), and beat-synced actions (open, spin, sway, paint burst). All derived from TB[] (bar times) and BEAT_B. Crowd() function handles walking, popping, closing, reflections deterministically.
how: Create a crowd.py module for 'street scene' templates (mythology processions, tech conference crowds). Input: beat grid, positions, color palette. Output: per-frame stroke lists for walkers, umbrellas, ribbons. Reuse figScale(y) perspective logic.

title: Glyph-Progress Prop Tracking
text: Character glyph strokes (SHUI) store centerline points with pressure. tipAt(strokes, stroke_idx, progress) returns interpolated brush-tip position. Sword tip follows this exactly during 'writing' animation, syncing prop to stroke reveal.
how: In plan.py, for any 'drawing/writing' scene, export glyph stroke data (JSON). In compose.py, animate prop (pen, sword, pointer) by sampling tipAt(progress) where progress comes from TTS-aligned caption timing.

title: Local Character Plate Coordinates
text: Each character plate defines local origin (GOX, GOY) and size (GRW, GRH) relative to scene. drawGirlBody/Head draw in local space. buildGirl() extracts strokes, then subtracts GOX/GOY from stroke coords for world placement. Clean separation of art coords from layout.
how: In compose.py, enforce Plate class: draw() receives local Ref (w,h). build_plate() returns strokes already translated to world (ox, oy). Eliminates ad-hoc coordinate math in scene functions.

title: Ink Bloom Transition Shader
text: WebGL reveal mask (comp.js revealM) expands a radial mask warped by FBM noise (0.55*large + 0.25*small). Edge adds a dark 'water-line' band (exp(-pow(...))). Transition mixes two full layer-sets (wet/dry/col) with independent paper offsets.
how: Port revealM GLSL to a HyperFrames custom filter (GSAP shader pass). Use for 'style change' transitions (e.g., Lab→Classic) where new style blooms from a point with organic edge.

title: Pose-Interpolation Stroke Rig
text: Poses are joint dicts (hip, shoulder, head, limbs, hem, sheath). mixPose recursively lerps numbers/arrays. Every frame, strokes regenerated from interpolated pose using fixed seed per stroke (stable bristle texture). Supports side/front/back views.
how: In a new avatar_talking_head.py, define key poses (neutral, speak_A, speak_B, gesture). Use mixPose(progress) per frame. Feed joint positions to stroke generator (or SVG morph) for deterministic, stylized 2D avatar.

title: Procedural Terrain Generation
text: land.js ridgeFn: generates mountain ridge polylines from [x, y, width] control points with cubic interpolation. mountainLayer(): renders layered parallax ridges with depth cueing (tone, mist, rim). Used for far/mid/near banks in wide/cross shots.
how: Add visual/terrain.py. In compose.py, generate background plates on-the-fly for 'establishing shot' scenes instead of hunting Muse images. Parameterize by mood (misty, sharp, dusk).

title: Shot-Specific Subtitle Positioning
text: shots.js exports subPos(id, t) returning [x, y, size] per VO line per shot (e.g., L1 at [170,860] on river bank, L3 at [1180,170] on cliff). Positions adapt to liubai composition. Main.js calls S.subPos(v.id, t) each frame.
how: Extend plan.py scene schema: add subtitle_anchor: {shot_id, x_pct, y_pct, size_rel}. compose_lab.py reads anchor per scene. Preflight.py validates anchor lies in low-detail region (liubai heuristic).

title: Procedural Wave & Water Motion
text: wave.js renders a giant pomo (泼墨) wave: wet ink mass body + 5 ink-loaded curling strokes (guide = face + lip) with feibai spray + Song-dynasty water lines + ink-dot foam. Parameters: rise (0-1), curl (0-1), time. Wave shape uses Catmull-Rom splines. Foam dots follow crest with sine sway.
how: Add WaveEffect to compose_lab.py for 'Aage Suno' flood scenes or Kaise Tech 'data tsunami' metaphor. Drive rise/curl from audio envelope (kick/snare). Render to offscreen canvas, composite with displacement.

title: Synthesized Foley & Instrument Stems
text: mix.py + score.py synthesize all audio from code: guqin/xiao/drums/pad stems via physical modelling (pluck.py, sampler.py); foley (drip, brush, water_step, splash, sword, cut, seal) via band-limited noise + sine envelopes. Precise event timeline (events.json) drives placement, ducking (−6 dB, 0.25 s smoothing), hard silence gates (digital zero), and loudness mastering. Self-check JSON validates onsets, RMS per section, silence floors.
how: Extend core/audio/sfx.py with synth_foley(type, gain, dur) and synth_score(stem, section) using the same numpy/scipy stack. Replace Pollinations/Muse audio search for Kaise Tech UI sounds and Puraan Ki Katha ritual effects. Add events.json export from plan.py for mix.py parity.

title: Two-Pass Line-Then-Fill Appearance
text: appear() draws each element twice per frame: first a line-art pass (fills = paper color) fading in over dLine=0.45s, then the coloured pass fading in over dFill=0.5s starting 0.8*dLine later. No part ever appears half-built or floating.
how: Implement in HyperFrames render loop: for each 'build' element (chart bar, diagram part), schedule two opacity keyframes — stroke-only then fill. Use in lab look for 'procedural build' sequences (e.g., PCB assembly, code structure reveal).

title: Procedural Hand Close-Up System
text: hand.js constructs a hand from 17 sphere hulls (palm, 4×3 phalanges, 2 thumb segments) with six preset poses (relaxed, flat, point, press, grip, pinch). Supports tipAt/palmAt placement, auto-sleeve extension to frame edge, and magnifier-circle clipping. Returns world wrist, palm, fingertips, and local axes.
how: Create a Python/Canvas port for magnifier shots in lab look: when script calls for 'press button', 'turn key', 'hold part', generate a close-up hand at 8× scale with correct pose. Integrate with compose_lab.py's magnifier component.

title: Pelvis-First Pose Weighting
text: Animate characters by treating the pelvis as the primary weight carrier. It shifts over the standing foot, drops for crouches, and dictates the 'hip roll' (dropping on the free-leg side). The chest then leans and twists relative to the pelvis.
how: In our animation plans, define the pelvis position first. Use the rule: `hipRoll = -hip_offset * 1.1` to automatically simulate natural weight distribution.

title: Biphonic Leg Shading
text: To prevent overlapping legs from merging into a single blob during walks or sits, automatically shade the 'far' leg (determined by depth/Z-index) 15-20% darker than the 'near' leg.
how: In the character render loop, calculate the average depth of the hip and knee for both legs. Apply a CSS filter or fill adjustment to the leg with the higher depth value.

title: Soft-Union Hairline Shader
text: Render hair as a region on a sphere using a soft union of two mathematical planes (back of skull and crown). This creates a rounded, natural hairline that follows head yaw/pitch/roll without needing separate assets for every angle.
how: Apply this logic in `compose_lab.py` when rendering character heads. Use the provided formula `m + log(exp(7*(a-m)) + exp(7*(b-m))) / 7` for the soft union edge.

title: Camera Keyframe Grammar (Drift/Gesture/Push/Cut/Follow/Punch)
text: CAM array defines keyframes with type: 'd' drift (easeInOut), 'g' gesture (custom gease: 0.45×eio + 0.55×eo), 'i' push-in (pow 2.4), 'c' cut (instant), 'f' follow (lerp to fn(t) with smoothstep weight), 'p' punch (easeOut). Rotation in degrees, zoom log-interpolated.
how: In compose_lab.py camera module, define keyframe objects with `kind` and `ease` fn. Implement follow: attach camera to moving element (e.g., chart bar top) via callback. Use punch for crack/impact moments (0.3 s easeOut).

title: Shared events.json for Audio-Visual Sync
text: events.json (generated by events.mjs) contains every mark: {t, d, type, pan, ...}. Consumed by mix.py (foley), video.mjs (render), and cuecheck.py (music hit-point audit). Single source of truth eliminates drift.
how: Modify plan.py to emit events.json alongside scene plan: each visual element (line, card, chart) gets entry with type (pencil/light/write/color/tap/gesture/morph/crack/grains/pour), timing, pan. mix.py and render read same file.

title: Dynamic Particle Systems for Grounds/Pour
text: DYN array holds per-frame draw functions. Grounds: 170 particles with quadratic bezier launch (control point random), scale decay, rotation, multiply blend, random coffee colors. Pour: bezier stream with animated noise displacement. Both use toScreen(cam) for camera-aware positioning.
how: Add DYN support in video.mjs / render loop. For lab look: data-flow particles (bezier from node to node), spark bursts on threshold break. Pass camera matrix to particle draw. Use multiply blend for additive feel. Seed RNG per particle for determinism.

title: Depth-sorted primitive queue with layer/depth/sequence
text: Engine queues draw calls as {depth, layer, seq, fn, state}. flush() sorts by layer → depth → seq, restores transform/alpha/keep per item, then executes. Guarantees correct occlusion for boxes, prisms, cylinders, text without a z-buffer. Sub-queues (sub()) allow interiors to render between back/front walls.
how: Replace HyperFrames' implicit paint order in compose.py/compose_lab.py with an explicit queue. Each scene element pushes {depth, layer, fn}; a single flush() sorts and draws. Fixes layering bugs when Ken Burns clips overlap cards/charts.

title: Animated pin label (dot → leader → text reveal)
text: pin(iso, x,y,z, {title, num, unit, dir, up, len, a}) draws in four staged fractions: dot pop (back-ease), leader up (eo), leader horizontal (eo), text clip-reveal (ss). Supports icons grid in the text row. All screen-space, anchored to a world point.
how: Add pin() to compose_lab.py for data callouts (model params, benchmark numbers). Call from plan.py with world coords of the panel/chart. Animate 'a' from 0→1 over 0.6s at station arrival. Replaces static captions with kinetic, spatially anchored labels.

title: Screen-space procedural bean field at high zoom
text: When camera k > 150, beanField() renders a tiled grid of rotated ellipses (3-tone shaded) anchored to a world point. Uses hash for per-bean variation, clips to a tear polygon during 'dive', fills frame at extreme zoom. O(tiles) but capped at 9000 tiles; falls back to flat fill.
how: In compose_lab.py, add a DetailField component: when camera zooms into a chart cell (k > threshold), render a procedural texture (dots for scatter, bars for histogram) anchored to that cell. Use for 'drill-down' moments in tech explainers.

title: Hero close-up billboards matching world style
text: palm(), cherry(), cup() in hero.js draw in screen-space billboards (world units → px via cam.k) using the same 3-tone palette and line weights as the isometric engine. Palm has articulated fingers (close param), cherry has highlight crescent, cup has animated steam. Identical geometry for opening/ending (0 km / 11,000 km tag).
how: Create a HeroBillboard class in compose_lab.py: takes a world anchor, renders a detailed 2D illustration (code editor, circuit, deity icon) at screen scale with lab-look styling. Use for 'detail dive' beats triggered by camera zoom threshold.

title: Animated route line with marching dashes
text: drawRoute(iso, u0, u1) draws a dashed polyline along a precomputed 3D route (ROUTE array with cumulative length). Dash offset = -t * lw * 4 so dashes march forward. Line width scales with cam.k. Always draws slightly ahead of story (routeLead(t)).
how: In compose_lab.py, add RouteLine component for 'journey' explainers (data pipeline, model training). Precompute route through stations; animate dash offset each frame. Shows progress without a separate progress bar.

title: Cut line with scissor tick (progressive reveal)
text: cutLine(g, pts, a) draws a dashed ink line along a polyline to fraction a, with a small filled circle at the head when a<1. Used for hull cut, box cut, sack tear. Timing synced to sound events (knife, tear).
how: Add to compose_lab.py for 'opening' transitions: cut open a panel to reveal interior, slice a chart to highlight a segment. Drive 'a' from timeline; emit 'knife' sound event at start.

title: Circular inset detail view with leader
text: inset(iso, ax,ay, cx,cy, r, a, drawIn) animates a leader line from anchor (ax,ay) to inset center (cx,cy), then grows a clipped disc (back-ease) with drop shadow and double ring. drawIn(g,cx,cy,R,progress) renders arbitrary content inside.
how: Use in compose_lab.py for 'zoom into metric' beats: anchor on a chart bar, inset shows breakdown table or formula. Animate 'a' over 0.8s at station arrival.

title: Isotype icon grid with fractional fill and pop-in
text: iconGrid(g, x,y, n, m, cols, gap, draw) lays out n icons in a grid; first m are 'lit' (full color), rest dim. Each lit icon gets a pop-in scale = back(clamp(m-i), 2.4). Supports fractional m (partial fill). Used for 21 suns (drying days), 14 containers, 18 day/night cycles, 70 beans in cup.
how: Add IconGrid to compose_lab.py for stat callouts: '14B params', '21 epochs', '70% accuracy'. Drive m from timeline (e.g., m = total * progress). Replaces static icon rows with animated counting.

title: Extruded 3D text on isometric planes
text: text3/text3Now renders a string on plane 'xy' (lying), 'xz' (standing facing +y), or 'yz' (standing facing +x) with extrusion. Each glyph drawn in steps: back faces (dark tone) → middle (mid tone) → front face (light tone). Supports custom triad, size, weight, tracking. Used for title card words (FROM BEAN TO CUP) and station labels.
how: Add ExtrudedText to compose_lab.py for section titles that live in 3D space (e.g., floating above a chart). Render via the depth queue so they occlude correctly with panels. Use 'xy' plane for floor labels, 'xz' for wall-mounted signs.

title: Shape extrusion from arbitrary 2D outline
text: shape(iso, pts, at, {scale, depth, color, plane}) takes a 2D polygon (pts in local xy), places it at world 'at', extrudes by depth on plane 'xy'/'xz'/'yz', shades sides by normal using the 3-tone triad. Includes sparkPath(n,r,inner) and cursorPath() as examples. Enables 'draw anything in this style'.
how: In compose_lab.py, add a CustomProp component: designer provides an SVG path → converted to pts → shape() extrudes it into an isometric prop (logo, icon, UI element). Shares the lab-look material system automatically.

title: Simulation-Driven Animation Pipeline
text: Boarding logic (72 pax, queue path, aisle blocking, stow time) simulated offline at 30fps into SIM[] frames (mode: gate/walk/stow/sit, position s). Render scrubs sim time via simT(t) per shot (real-time, time-lapse, rewind). Decouples complex logic from render loop; ensures consistency across shots; enables fast-forward/rewind.
how: In plan.py/research.py, for process explainers (logistics, algorithms, physics), write a sim.py that outputs JSON frames (state per entity per dt). In compose_lab.py, add a SimScrubber component that maps video time → sim frame → entity props. Use for crowd scenes, traffic, sorting visualizations.

title: Floor-Plane Kinetic Typography System
text: phraseLayout(P) measures each glyph (via OffscreenCanvas), assigns appear time tc (step=0.14s), line gap, indent. floorType(g,t,P,L) renders on world plane 'xy' via onPlane() transform: each glyph pops in (eo easing), scales down from 1.22→1, color shifts from ghost→ink. phraseBox/PhraseWorld give screen-space bounds for readcheck.
how: Build floor_type.py: input text blocks + world position → generate per-glyph animation data (tc, u, v, size, color). Render in HyperFrames via <g> with transform='matrix3d(...)' for ground plane. Use phraseBox for preflight.py margin audit. Supports Hinglish (NotoSerifSC) + Latin (Newsreader) mixed runs.

title: Minimal People Billboard System (Walk/Stow/Sit)
text: drawPerson(g,p,pose) and drawSeated(g,p) render billboards in world units (seen from behind, no faces). Pose: {phase, walking, bag, lift, caseUp}. Walk cycle: leg swing sin(phase), body bob |cos|. Stow: lift 0→1 over 0.3, arc up, lower in. Sit: cross-fade standing→seated at seat coords. Hair/hat/skin variants per agent.
how: Add PeopleBillboard class to compose_lab.py. Pre-render sprite sheets (walk 8 frames, stow 6, sit 4) at 4 angles using engine.js person() offscreen. At runtime, pick frame by pose.phase. Use for crowd scenes in Puraan Ki Katha / Aage Suno. Low cost vs 3D rigs.

title: Procedural Isometric Geometry Kit (Extrude/Loft/Hinge)
text: `plane.js` demonstrates a complete parametric kit: ellipse sections (`ell`, `arc`), `extrude(section, y0, y1)` for hull walls, `loft(stations)` for tapered nose/tail, `lidMap(hinge, rot, dx,dy,dz)` for flap animation. All facets drawn with `facet(g, quad, material, {out, color})` using painter's algorithm. Deterministic, no 3D engine.
how: Extract `kit.js` primitives (`extrude`, `loft`, `facet`, `iso.P`) into `hyperframes/kit.js`. Use for `compose_lab.py` 'object props on black' (server racks, PCB boards, device hulls). Replace ad-hoc shape code with parametric sections. Enables 'CAD-to-Video Pipeline' brain item.

title: Shake Hits Array for Impact Feedback
text: `HITS = [[time, amplitude], ...]` drives a `shake(t)` function: damped oscillation (exp(-d*14)*amp * sin/cos) applied as canvas transform translation. Used for slams, stamps, freezes, verdicts. Cheap, effective 'screen juice' locked to audio events.
how: Add `HITS` to `events.json` (type `shake`). In `compose.py` render loop, compute `shake(t)` and apply `ctx.translate(sx, sy)` before drawing frame. Amplitude calibrated per event type (slam=16, stamp=8, freeze=10).

title: Subtitle Safe-Area Width Gate in Headless Browser
text: Tool (cues.mjs) loads the film page, measures each bilingual subtitle line (Chinese 40px SC + English 28px Oswald) with `canvas.measureText`, ensures total width ≤ 1880px (1920 frame - margins), fails build if any line overflows. Runs in seconds.
how: Add to `preflight.py` or `review.py`. Reuse `thumb.py`/`compose.py` font loading (NotoSansSC-sub.woff2, Oswald). Render subtitle DOM/text in a hidden canvas at 1920w, measure, assert. Block render if `bad > 0`.

title: VO Duration Drift Gate (TTS vs Timeline)
text: `vo_lengths.py` loads `dur.json` (actual TTS file durations) and `VO_DUR` from `film.js`, flags any line where `abs(actual - planned) > 0.08s`. Edge-TTS/Kokoro drift is common; >80ms desyncs visuals. Fails build.
how: Add to `voice_gate` in `plan.py`/`pace.py`. After TTS generation (`tts.py`), write `dur.json`. Before render, run this check. If drift, either re-synthesize with adjusted speed or update `VO_DUR` in `events.json`/`film.js` automatically.

title: Wikimedia Commons Source Fetcher with Rate-Limit Retry
text: `cq.py` + `fetch_sources.sh`: Commons API search/category/info with exponential backoff (15s * attempt) on 429. `SOURCES.jsonl` lists `{file, url, license}`. Shell script downloads serially, sleeps 3s between, verifies file size. Guarantees legal, high-res archive footage.
how: Add `tools/cq.py` and `fetch_sources.sh` to repo. Create `SOURCES.jsonl` for each page (Puraan Ki Katha, Kaise Tech). Run in `build.sh` before render. Use `license` field for `Archive Footage License Auditor` brain item.

title: Data-Driven On-Screen Numbers Measured from Primary Source
text: Every statistic shown on screen (point count, wall length, canopy height %, area km²) is computed in build_data.py from the raw LiDAR/NAIP data and written to facts.json. The render and overlay code reads facts.json — no hard-coded numbers. This eliminates hallucination and allows instant updates when data changes.
how: In research.py, after Gemini watches top Shorts, also run a fact-extraction pass that writes a facts.json for the topic (counts, dates, measurements). Modify compose.py / compose_lab.py to read facts.json for any on-screen data plates, counters, or charts. Store facts.json in the video's unit folder.

title: Circular Clip-Path Light/Dark Transition
text: Two full-screen world layers (light/dark) stacked; the top layer gets clip-path: circle(r px at cx cy) where radius expands from the triggering UI element (e.g., toggle button) at 3200 px/s. Reverse transition uses same logic. Runs entirely in browser CSS, no canvas shader needed.
how: In compose_lab.py / HyperFrames template, render light and dark DOM trees simultaneously. On theme-switch event, apply expanding clip-path to the outgoing layer via GSAP. Center (cx,cy) = anchor coordinates of the switch element.

title: Pixel-Block Sweep Chapter Wipe
text: Chapter transition: 32×18 grid of 60 px blocks. Each block scales from 0→1 with a diagonal delay (bottom-left to top-right) using per-block hash jitter. Blocks hold at full size while chapter title fades in, then scale out in same direction. A tiny pixel character runs across the middle during the hold.
how: Add wipe() to transition library in compose_lab.py. Drive by a single progress uniform (0-1). Use existing 'chapter' events from playbook.md to trigger. Keeps the 'lab' pixel aesthetic.

title: Deterministic Typing Simulation with Jitter & SFX Events
text: typing(t0, text, cps, seed) returns per-character timestamps. Interval = (1/cps) * (0.55 + hash*0.9) + space_pause(0.03) + punctuation_pause(0.12). Emits 'key'/'tkey' events with velocity for SFX. First character at -0.6 s (silence padding) clipped to 0.
how: Replace current terminal typing in compose_lab.py with this function. Feed timestamps into GSAP timeline for character reveals. Pass 'key' events to events.json for mix.py SFX sync. Seed = line index for reproducibility.

title: Integrated HUD Overlay System
text: Single HUD object per frame composites: subtitles (emphasis via <em>), chapter tags (number+name), keystroke hints (keycap graphics + label, appear 1.5 s before shortcut), 4× speed label (blinking ▶▶), radial spotlight (on key UI element), screenshot flash + toast, fade-in/out. All driven by timeline events, rendered in browser overlay layer.
how: Extend hud.py / review.py to generate a HUD spec per frame from events.json. Render in HyperFrames as a fixed top layer (z-index 10). Use existing 'keys', 'chapter', 'ramp', 'spot', 'flash', 'toast' event types.

title: Declarative UI State Machine for Simulated App Recording
text: Full app UI (terminal, file tree, plan pane, diff view, preview, split-screen) defined as nested data structures (appState) updated per frame from timeline. No real app or screen recording needed. Elements have enter/exit animations (back/elastic ease), loading states, tool call spinners, diff line highlights, comment threads, CI logs.
how: In plan.py / compose_lab.py, define UI scenes as JSON state trees (like film.js appState). Render via HyperFrames components. Timeline events ('pane', 'tool', 'read', 'write', 'send', 'split') mutate state. Enables 'lab look' explainers without OBS.

title: Terrain Cross-Section Profile Extraction for Map Shorts
text: Given a polyline (wall/river/road), sample LiDAR/DEM points within a 7 m offset strip. Project to along-track/offset coordinates. Detrend each cross-section (linear fit on outer shoulders >3.5 m). Bin offsets at 0.5 m, compute median elevation. Output: height (max median), FWHM (width at 50% height), base width (width at 15% height), median profile array.
how: Add profile.py logic to scout.py for Puraan Ki Katha map segments. Use open DEM (SRTM/COP30) via rasterio. Generate profile JSON → feed to compose_lab.py 'line chart' or 'stat counter' components for 'wall height 0.5 m, length 3.4 km' visuals.

title: Event-Driven Ambience Bed with Probability & Swell
text: Ambience layers (waves, gulls, crickets, creaks) are scheduled from events.json with time-varying gain envelopes (e.g., waves swell 0.5→1.0 at night) and per-trigger probability (crickets 75% every 0.31s). Uses brown noise + bandpass for waves, synthesized gull/crickets/creaks.
how: In mix.py, replace static ambience loops with event-driven scheduler: read 'amb' events from events.json, each with what, start, duration, gain envelope function, and probability. Synthesize on the fly. Keeps ambience reactive to picture.

title: Per-Line Voice Speed Control
text: lines.json includes a 'speed' field per line (0.86–0.92). TTS honors this for natural pacing variation — slower for emphasis, faster for lists. Combined with word-level offsets, gives fine prosody control without SSML.
how: Add 'speed' to lines.json schema. Pass to tts.py (Gemini TTS supports speaking_rate). Use in plan.py to auto-assign: hook lines 0.85, body 0.95, climax 0.88. Verify in pace.py.

title: Deterministic seeded audio synthesis
text: All randomness in synthesis (partial phases, noise bursts, reverb tail) uses a single fixed seed (e.g., 20260925). Guarantees bit-identical renders across runs, enabling reliable caching and diffing.
how: Set a global RNG seed in score.py and any stochastic audio processes. Store seed in brain.jsonl per video for reproducibility.

title: Tilt-shift miniature look via post-process
text: A separable blur pass blurs top and bottom of frame (band around focal line) with variable radius, simulating a miniature model. Implemented as a shader pass after bloom, before color grade.
how: Add a CSS filter or WebGL post-pass in HyperFrames for 'lab' look videos needing a macro/miniature aesthetic. Control focal line (fy) and band width per scene via style config.

title: Focus-line and speed-line primitives for motion emphasis
text: kit.js focus(cx,cy,rx,ry,n,seed) draws n radial ink triangles from ellipse to outer radius. speed(x0,y0,w,h,ang,n,seed,t,v) draws horizontal streaks with random length/width, moving at velocity v (px/s). Both seeded, deterministic, boil at 12fps.
how: Add focus_lines() and speed_lines() to HyperFrames primitives. Use in lab look for 'camera shutter' moments, 'light runs', 'crowd blur'. Control via beat events (amplitude → n, v).

title: Procedural sound-effect lettering (sfx) with per-glyph physics
text: kit.js sfx() draws Japanese-style sound words: each glyph gets random rotation, offset, triple stroke (ink/rim/fill), scale-in bounce (back easing), and 12 Hz boil jitter. Layout follows a path (straight, curved, vertical) with staggered entrance (0.03s/glyph). Returns screen bbox for readcheck.
how: Add sfx() to kit.ts (port from kit.js). Call from compose_lab.py for onomatopoeia (e.g., 'धड़क', 'झप') at beat-synchronized moments. Register bboxes in TX for preflight audit.

title: Prop-swap pipeline for consistent asset iteration
text: gen_camswap.sh moves old prop images to gen/before/, regenerates the prop alone (prod_hero_redesign), then re-edits each dependent image using the old image as base and new prop as second reference. Prompt includes 'how the camera is held' line. Anchors re-measured after.
how: Add a swap_prop.py script: take old asset list, new prop prompt, run image-to-image edit with two refs (old asset, new prop). Update anchor JSON (A.key.u/v etc.) via a quick vision check. Use for product updates in Kaise Tech.

title: Flipbook page-turn animation for photo sequences
text: flipPage(k, lt) draws a book page with a single frame of animation (character landing, pigeons scattering). S_c5 renders 30 pages in 1s: top page lifts from right edge (fold line slanted), reveals next page underneath, back of lifted page shows mirrored content. Page edges show thickness.
how: Implement flipbook() in compose_lab.py for 'photo dump' sequences. Feed generated keyframes as pages. Use 30fps, 1s duration. Add page-flip foley (mix.py flip()).

title: Glowing ribbon primitive for routes/lanes/pipelines (world-width + screen-width, flow, dash, head, wake)
text: Single `ribbon(pts, opts)` function creates a triangle strip along a polyline. Vertex shader expands by `max(worldWidth, pixelWidth * distance)`. Fragment shader supports: flow (marching dashes), head (glowing tip), dash/duty, wake (trailing glow per ship), soft reveal (`revA`/`revB`), intensity. Used for tanker routes, TSS lanes, pipelines, globe routes. Additive blending, no depth write.
how: Implement in GSAP/SVG: `Ribbon` class taking points + options. Animate `revB` (reveal), `flowPh` (march), `head` (pulse) on beat. Use for shipping lanes, migration routes, supply chains, data flows. Style: amber glow (`#ffc36b`), ice edges (`#d9e6ee`), wake (`#fff1dc`).

title: Growing data pillar animation (slabs appear on beat, fractional Y-scale)
text: Pillar = stack of cylinders (slabs). `growPillar(p, n, k)` shows `n*k` slabs; each slab scales Y from 0 to 1, position adjusts to keep base grounded. Big pillar: 20 slabs (1M bbl each) grow over 2.4 s (one per beat-eighth). Small pillars: fractional heights (2.6, 3.5, 2.0) with lighter top segment for range. Edge rings highlight each slab.
how: Add `Pillar` component to `compose_lab.py` / GSAP. Data: `{value: 20, unit: 'M bbl/d', slabHeight: 5.5, color: 0xffb04a}`. Animate `slabCount` with `ease: 'power2.out'` on beat grid. Show tick labels every 5 slabs. Use for oil, remittances, subscribers, GDP — any 'stack' metric.

title: Cross-section cutaway shader (clip plane + exaggerated depth + lane markers)
text: Custom shader discards fragments on camera side of a moving plane (`cutP`, `cutD`). Fragment shader renders rock (brown), water (teal→navy with 25 m depth lines), sea floor (strata). Lanes drawn as amber bands at correct depth positions. Vertical exaggeration: land ×3.2, water depth ×150. Camera orbits section line; labels (INBOUND/OUTBOUND, depth) appear on beat.
how: Simulate in 2.5D: `compose_lab.py` adds `CrossSection` scene. Use two layers (land/water) masked by animated clip-path. Draw depth lines with GSAP `drawSVG`. Animate lane markers sliding in. Exaggeration factors as config. Voice cue: 'water depth ×150 · land ×3.2' stamp.

title: Globe-to-map dissolve with matched frustums and atmosphere flash
text: Two cameras (PerspectiveCamera map/globe). `mapToGlobe(t)` inverts map camera position to globe lat/lon/alt. Dissolve 5.6→6.4 s and 40.0→40.8 s: cross-fade `gW` (globe weight), render both to offscreen, blend. Warm atmosphere flash (`rgba(232,214,180, 0.22*sin(π*gW))`) at midpoint. Globe camera uses `setViewOffset` for off-center composition during pull-back.
how: Implement in HyperFrames: `GlobeMapTransition` component. Pre-calc matching keyframes for 'orbit' and 'dive'. Use two canvases (or pre-rendered globe video + live map). Cross-fade with additive flash frame. Add to `compose_lab.py` transitions list (currently 3 rotating).

title: Ruler/measure visual grammar (animated line with tick marks, labels on beat)
text: At 21.3–22.1 s: ruler line draws across two lanes (5 NM total). Four tick marks appear sequentially (0.18 s apart). Labels ('INBOUND·2 NM', 'BUFFER·2 NM', 'OUTBOUND·2 NM') fade in at midpoints. Line draws with `eio` easing. Click SFX per tick. All synced to beat grid.
how: Add `Ruler` component to `compose_lab.py`. Config: `startPt`, `endPt`, `segments: [{label, color, width}]`. Animate line `drawSVG` 0→1, ticks `scaleY` 0→1, labels `opacity` 0→1 on beat offsets. Use for 'gap', 'distance', 'capacity', 'time' comparisons. Style: amber ticks, dim buffer, light labels.

title: Reproducible asset bake scripts (fetch → prep → bake → fonts → cues) with manifest logging
text: Each tool (`fetch.py`, `prep.py`, `bake.py`, `fonts.py`, `cues.py`) is a standalone CLI writing to `raw/` and `assets/`. `manifest.jsonl` logs every URL fetch (bytes, date). `bbox.json`/`wbbox.json` store projection params for alignment. `build.sh` (referenced) orchestrates full render with `?t0=&t1=` for segments. No manual steps.
how: Create `tools/` dir in our repo. Port `fetch.py` (OSM, terrain, imagery), `prep.py` (crop, grade, mask), `bake.py` (shadows), `fonts.py` (subset), `cues.py` (subs). Add `build.sh` calling `python -m tools.fetch`, `python -m tools.prep`, `node render.js --t0 0 --t1 52`. Log to `manifest.jsonl`. Enables CI/CD and asset audit.

title: Diegetic Torn-Paper Subtitle Prop (Bilingual + Jittered Edges)
text: Subtitles are a torn slip of the same paper texture laid at bottom: Chinese (LXGW) over English (Kalam), 78% opacity English. Torn edges = per-scanline jitter (±3.5 px) seeded by line ID. Paper fill = rgba(251,250,247,.96) with subtle stroke. No safe-area box — it *is* the paper.
how: In thumb.py / compose_lab.py caption layer, replace box with drawTornSlip(ctx, zh, en, y=948). Use mulberry32(id) for edge jitter. Load paper texture pattern. Set font stack: LXGW 38px / Kalam 31px. Add to style config for 'marker-paper' page.

title: Multiplicative ink density compositing
text: Strokes and letters add to per-colour 'lighter' layers; final composite multiplies paper RGB by (1 - ink_transmittance)^(1+0.6*(overlaps-1)) so crossings darken like real marker without blowing out to black.
how: In compose_lab.py, replace alpha-over with a density layer per accent colour (black/red/blue) and apply the power-law transmittance at composite time; keeps Ken Burns photos clean while making diagram overlaps feel tactile.

title: Halftone dots in shadow regions
text: In shadowed fragments (shadowMap > 0.5), overlay a world-space hexagonal dot screen (scale 0.38) that brightens the deep-indigo shadow by 45% where dots hit, mimicking print halftone without extra passes.
how: Add a 'halftone_shadow' flag to lab-look panel specs; in compose_lab.py's composite step, for pixels with shadow>0.5, mix in a deterministic dot pattern (hash-based) at 0.38 world scale before loudnorm.

title: Hard-edged lamp pool night lighting
text: Night shader darkens everything to indigo-violet; each lamp contributes a hard-edged warm circle (aaStep radius falloff + height falloff) blended additively; window panes emit only when wave has passed and night>0.5.
how: For evening/dark lab scenes, add lamp_pool[] to events.json (x,y,z,radius,colour); in compose_lab.py composite, apply night tint then add radial gradients for each pool; gate window glows with same wave-passed logic.

title: Glyph-skeleton handwriting pipeline
text: Precompute centre-line skeletons for every glyph (Zhang-Suen thinning + RDP simplification) into JSON; at render time stroke each polyline with a fat mask (destination-in) so letters appear stroke-by-stroke in the actual font shape.
how: Add tools/skeleton.py to our bake step; feed Kalam/LXGW subsets; store skeletons in brain.jsonl; extend compose_lab.py caption renderer to draw via skeleton paths instead of fillText for handwritten captions and diagram labels.

title: Identical transition signature across sections
text: Every seasonal change (3× in 45s) uses the exact same 3-part audio-visual signature: big tree squat (muffled thump) → spring back (boing) → rising harp run + whoosh. Creates a memorable, predictable 'chapter marker' that viewers learn to anticipate.
how: Design a signature transition for our series (e.g., Kaise Tech 'lab' shorts): a 1.5s audio-visual motif (SFX + visual) that plays at every major topic shift. Implement in compose_lab.py as a reusable 'chapter_wipe' component triggered by events.json.

title: Blueprint/cyanotype progressive line drawing renderer
text: Cyanotype paper texture, four line weights (outline/detail/thin/hair), dashed centre/hidden lines, dimension lines with arrows and extension lines, handwritten annotations, single red stamp. Lines draw progressively stroke-by-stroke (global DRAW 0..1). Includes title block and detail callouts.
how: Implement a 'blueprint' scene type in compose_lab.py for tech-spec shorts (Kaise Tech). Use Canvas 2D path drawing with draw progress; feed DRAW from timeline. Adds a high-authority visual metaphor for diagrams, schematics, 'how it works' segments.

title: Static first/last frame caching for segment transitions
text: Cache first and last frames of each game/stage segment (render once, reuse) to composite TV-frame transitions (push-in/out, slot-machine reels, boss collage) without re-rendering complex scenes. Reduces render time and ensures pixel-perfect match cuts.
how: In our HyperFrames render pipeline (video.mjs equivalent), add a frame cache keyed by segment ID + timestamp. Before rendering a transition, check cache for source/target frames. Use for Ken Burns handoffs, card flips, and 'lab look' panel transitions.

title: Character consistency across visual styles
text: The same character (Dot) appears in risograph, crayon, ink, pixel, blueprint, ASCII, and Swiss styles with identical proportions, antenna ball, helmet, and expression logic (face: determined/panic/idea/ah/sneeze/happy/proud). Each style module implements its own cadetXxx() but shares a canonical expression timeline driven by local time.
how: Create a character_spec.json defining canonical proportions, expression keyframes, and prop attachments. Each look (classic, lab, new styles) gets a renderer that consumes this spec. Plan.py validates expression continuity across cuts. Preflight checks silhouette match.

title: ASR-verified subtitle lines with trim/asr fields
text: lines.json includes id, timestamp, speaker, text, voice, speed, and optional trim (short form for command words) and asr (expected recognition). The pipeline generates lines.json.asr.json with ASR results for verification. FX lines marked fx:true for sound-effect treatment.
how: Update research.py and plan.py to output lines.json with trim/asr/fx fields. Voice gate compares ASR output to asr field; mismatch > 10% triggers re-TTS. Subtitle burner uses trim for command-word overlays. Stats.py logs ASR pass rate.

title: Deterministic scene test harness with URL params
text: main.js supports ?test=chars, ?test=fonts, ?scene=g_boss.testBoss for isolated visual regression. Each scene exports testXxx(g, t) drawing a fixed timestamp. Fonts preloaded via document.fonts.load(). Enables instant visual QA without full render pipeline.
how: Add a --test flag to render.py that loads a headless Chromium, navigates to file:///compose.html?scene=MODULE.FUNC&t=TIME, captures PNG, and compares to golden master (pixelmatch ≤ 0.1%). Integrate into doctor.py pre-commit.

title: HUD component library (fuse, command, stamp, lives, subtitle)
text: Reusable canvas components: fuse timer (braided cord + spark + beat knots), command word (slam-in, hold, shrink-to-tag), result stamp (OK/OOPS pop), life icons (crack/fall animation), subtitle plate (gold rounded rect + icon). All take (g, time, params) and handle their own enter/exit curves.
how: Port to HyperFrames as GSAP timelines in hud_components.js: FuseBar, CommandWord, ResultStamp, LifeRow, SubtitlePlate. Each exposes .play(startTime, config). Compose_lab.py imports and places them on the lab HUD layer. Review.py checks subtitle safe-area and command-word legibility.

title: Ink-wash parachute deployment with feibai and jiaomo
text: inkCanopy() animates a single ink drop → blot → 9-panel canopy with alternating dark/light panels, wavy hem, feibai (dry-brush streaks) at edges, and shroud lines. Growth controlled by single grow 0..1 param. Dust (jiaomo) and splatter layered with multiply composite. All procedural, no sprites.
how: Add ink_parachute.ts to lab look: a GSAP-driven SVG/Canvas component that takes grow (0-1), hem position, scale, and renders the same phases. Use for any 'deploy' metaphor (parachute, airbag, sail). Preflight checks panel count ≤ 9 and grow monotonic.

title: True Silence Gating in Music Stems
text: score.py applies gate() to drums/bass/brass/keys/jingles during designated silence ranges (10ms ramps). Only 'color' stem (guqin, heartbeat, drone) remains audible. Creates dramatic 'vacuum' moments without digital silence.
how: In score.py / mix.py, define silence ranges in timeline.json (e.g., S7_dark, BOSS_silence). During mix, multiply non-color stems by envelope that ramps to 0. Keep foley/voice unaffected.

title: Hard-Shadow Cartoon Primitive Library (toon.js)
text: toon.js provides part() (fill → clip → shift → light fill → outline), tube() (double-stroke limbs), outlined() (bold UI text), limb() (2-segment IK), smooth() (Catmull-Rom). All line widths scale with K.s for constant screen thickness.
how: Port part/tube/outlined/limb to Python/GSAP for HyperFrames lab look. Use for HUD elements, character rigs, UI panels. Ensures consistent 'lab' aesthetic across code-generated visuals.

title: TTS Single-Word Artifact Trim via Whisper Timestamps
text: trim_cmd.py detects one-word commands (Pump, Zip, Land) that Kokoro/Gemini TTS tails with extra vowels. Uses faster-whisper word timestamps to find first word end, cuts at lowest-energy point within 80 ms, applies 40 ms fade-out. Updates dur.json and lines.json with asr/trim fields.
how: Integrate into tts.py post-generation: for any line where text.split() == 1 and not fx, run whisper base.en word timestamps, trim, rewrite wav and dur.json. Add asr field to lines.json for subs.py.

title: Font Version Pinning for Reproducible Renders
text: fonts.sh fetches Google Fonts from a pinned commit hash (86aced91de05cd4f96a06838124cca45be337b2b) via raw.githubusercontent.com. Skips if file exists; FORCE=1 re-fetches. Ensures identical glyph metrics across machines/time.

title: Data-verified script numbers against source measurements
text: export.mjs loads plates.json/nucleus.json, computes tissue_mm, collagen %, ratio, nucleus_um from raw scan data, and asserts equality with NUM constants in timeline.js. Any mismatch fails the build.
how: In plan.py, after Gemini writes the script, add a verification step that extracts all claimed numbers (specs, percentages, sizes) and cross-checks them against the research.json primary sources (API responses, PDF tables). Fail or flag before TTS.

title: Measurement-based visual grammar (scale bars, dimension lines from data)
text: Microscope demo draws a dimension line along the tissue's true long axis (PCA on tissue mask), shows '4.8 mm' from plates.json. Two measuring circles (1 mm diameter) reveal collagen % via a half-plane scan front synced to cumulative histogram. Nucleus ring fits 72-ray edge detection. Every visual number is a direct measurement.
how: For Kaise Tech explainers citing specs (battery mAh, sensor µm, latency ms), draw ruler/measure primitives (animated line with tick marks, labels on beat) using the actual numbers from research.json. Use the 'Ruler/measure visual grammar' brain entry: animate line growth on beat, snap labels to grid.

title: Iris transitions through focal medallions
text: Step transitions use circular iris centered on previous step's medallion (focus point) expanding to full frame over 0.9 beat (ease-in-out). Payoff section opens with iris from start-button center (pressIris). Iris radius: lerp(104, 1250, k²). Medallion number flashes at center during first half.
how: In compose.py transition logic, when next section is 'step', capture previous scene's focus point (medallion center). Render outgoing scene clipped to expanding circle at that point. Render incoming scene inside same circle. Use k² for faster initial expansion. Flash step number at center while k<0.5.

title: Mantel clock ambience on half-note grid
text: Quiet wood_tick (0.03 gain) placed every 2 beats (half-note) throughout, except during motor-owned payoff section (21.2–27.3s). Pan -0.6. Creates subliminal tempo glue. Clock stops exactly during climax, returns after.
how: In mix.py ambience section, add loop placing wood_tick at k*2*BEAT. Skip ranges from events.json where type='motor' or 'climax'. Gain -30dB (0.03), pan -0.6. Ensures tempo perception even in quiet sections. Add to style config as 'tempo_clock' toggle.

title: Swing timing helper for beat-synced animation
text: T(bar, beat, swing=0.6) converts musical position to seconds: beat 0.5 (off-beat) maps to 60% of beat duration. Automatically handles swung eighths so animation keyframes lock to swing grid without manual offset math.
how: Add T() to shared timing module (pace.py or new timing.py). Use in compose_lab.py for kinetic titles, stat counters, panel transitions that need swing feel. Pass swing ratio from music metadata.

title: Procedural brick/tile facade textures in shader
text: Fragment shader generates brick walls (staggered rows, jittered mortar, per-brick color variation) and mosaic tiles (beveled edges, grout lines) from world coordinates. No textures needed. Grime, rain streaks, wetness modulated by noise. Building metadata (type, tint, roof height) passed via uniform array `bld[8]`.
how: If moving to WebGL/Canvas2D shaders for lab look, port `facade()` and `tile()` GLSL to GSAP/Canvas custom shaders or use as reference for procedural SVG/Canvas patterns.

title: Neon tube glyph pipeline from font skeleton
text: Hand-lay neon tube centrelines on Noto Sans SC skeleton (10x10 grid) and Latin caps (10-high). Each glyph = list of units (one bent tube each); each unit = polylines joined by black-painted double-backs (single-point strokes). Export `glyphs.json`. Build script fetches OFL fonts, subsets hanzi, runs `glyphs_build.py` to trace skeleton -> tube paths.
how: Add `tools/glyphs_build.py` to generate `glyphs.json` for Hinglish/English titles. Use in `thumb.py` or `compose_lab.py` for neon-style end cards.

title: Event list generation from timeline data
text: Function `evList()` walks all sign circuits, cat keyframes, fish keyframes, and timeline markers `T` to emit `events.json` with `{t, type, circ, gas, pan, dur, ...}`. Types: strike, off, spark, fill, purr, step, land, swat, spin, rain, crack, leak, drain, glug, flop, die, fizz, hush, dive, grab, chorus, drop, splash, revive, close, sleep, lastdrop, card, peek. Pan computed by projecting circuit center through current camera.
