title: Neon Gas Colour Palette with Phosphor-Coat Flag
text: Physical gas colours: neon=[1.0,0.11,0.035], argon=[0.24,0.46,1.0], plus phosphor-coated variants (green, white, pink, purple, turquoise, yellow). Clear glass tubes use gas colour directly; coated tubes use phosphor colour.
how: Map to CSS gradient stops in compose_lab.py neon components; add `coat` boolean to tube props for authentic look in Kaise Tech lab shorts.

title: Polyline Filleting with Leg-Proportional Radius Clamping
text: Round interior corners with quadratic arcs; radius = min(requested, 0.45 * legA, 0.45 * legB). Prevents overshoot on tight corners and mimics real glass bending limits. Implemented in lib.js fillet() with quadratic Bezier sampling (6 segments per 90°).
how: Add to HyperFrames path utils; use for neon-stroke reveals, kinetic title underlines, and HUD line animations in compose_lab.py.

title: Arc-Length Parameterization for Precise Stroke Animation
text: Precompute cumulative lengths (cumlen), then at(s) returns point + unit tangent; sub(s0,s1) extracts sub-path. Enables exact grow/dash/marching-ants by arc length, not parameter t.
how: Integrate into HyperFrames path module; drive neon drawing reveals, progress bars, and route-line marching dashes with beat-synced arc-length keys.

title: Procedural Facade Generation with Seeded Types
text: Buildings defined as [x0,x1,type,seed] with type 0=brick,1=mosaic,2=plaster; tint per building. Shopfronts: win/door/shutter with lit colour per group. Upper windows pseudo-randomly lit via (i*7+round(y))%5==1. Alleys are near-black slots.
how: Create `facade.js` module for HyperFrames; generate background city blocks for establishing shots in Puraan Ki Katha and Kaise Tech.

title: Electrode Gap Splitting for Authentic Neon Ends
text: Closed contour split at electrode point with 3 cm painted sleeves (caps). `split_loop(contour, cut_at, gap)` removes gap segment; first/last 3 cm of lit ranges become painted (dark). Double-backs routed behind lit strokes.
how: Implement in tubeFromStrokes for all neon text; ensures realistic electrode gaps in kinetic titles and end-card handles.

title: Smooth-Union SDF Blending (Polynomial smin)
text: Blend SDF primitives with `smin(a,b,k) = lerp(b,a,h) - k*h*(1-h)` where `h=clamp(0.5+0.5*(b-a)/k,0,1)`. k=0.022 for body parts, 0.016 for fish. Avoids hard edges in marching-squares extraction.
how: Add to SDF utility for procedural blobby shapes (ink blobs, water splashes, organic UI panels) in compose_lab.py shaders.

title: Contour Cleanup Pipeline: RDP → Resample → Laplacian Smooth
text: Marching-squares loops → Douglas-Peucker (eps=0.0012) → resample to uniform step (0.005m) → 3-iteration Laplacian smoothing (closed). Produces clean, animate-ready polylines.
how: Wrap as `cleanContour(loop)` in HyperFrames; apply to all vectorized assets (Muse SVG traces, FLUX edge maps) before animation.

title: Corner AI-generation disclosure tag
text: Top-left corner tag (330×64px) shows 'ILLUSTRATION / 示意 · AI 生成画面' whenever an AI-generated plate is visible. Gold left bar, mono label, SC Chinese. Appears only during plate shots (6–13s, 20–24s). Ethical transparency baked into visual grammar.
how: In compose_lab.py, add a CornerTag component that activates when scene uses AI-generated asset (flag in asset manifest). Text: 'ILLUSTRATION / AI-GENERATED' (EN) or '示意 · AI 生成画面' (Hinglish). Style: dark bg rgba(18,20,23,.82), gold left bar 8px, mono 18px + SC 20px. Position 96,56.

title: Data-driven chart components with real measurements
text: Three reusable chart types: (1) Kospi line chart — 19 daily closes plotted as % from Sep 23 peak, bear-market line at −20%, losing-streak counter increments on each new low. (2) Chip stock falling bars — two bars grow downward to −9.48%/−11.06%, reference line at −9% appears after both exceed it. (3) Spec ratio bar — total params (816B) full-width paper bar vs active params (42B) lemon bar, 5% badge auto-calculated.
how: Create ChartComponents module in HyperFrames: LineChart(data, peakIndex, bearThreshold), FallingBars(labels, values, refLine), RatioBar(total, active, unit='B'). Feed from research.py's fact-checked numbers. Animate on beat grid using existing GSAP timeline.

title: Persistent Subtitle Title Strip
text: Draw a dark gradient band (bottom 180px) that stays visible across cues, fading only during gaps >1s. Render bilingual subtitles (native script top, English bottom) with stroke inside band. Merge cue intervals if gap <1s to prevent blinking.
how: In compose.py subtitle renderer, compute SUBSPAN by merging intervals with gap <1s; draw band before subtitles; use SUB.zh/SUB.en fonts with stroke; position at H-82 / H-38.

title: Period Voice Treatment Chain
text: Apply a 1930s optical-track effect: bandpass 260–3700 Hz, +4 dB presence peak at 1.5–2.3 kHz, tanh distortion (carbon mic), wow/flutter (0.55 Hz + 6.3 Hz), early reflections (31 ms, 67 ms). Runs on clean TTS output before mixing.
how: Add period_voice() in mix.py after TTS load; use scipy.signal for filters, numpy.interp for wow/flutter; blend with music/foley via ducking envelope.

title: Animated Map with Albers Projection & Route Arcs
text: Project GeoJSON states via Albers equal-area (parallels 29.5°/45.5°, center -96°/37.5°). Draw dotted quadratic Bézier arcs between cities; pulse stars on hit; screen-space labels stay readable during zoom; odometer year counter rolls on beat.
how: In prep.py, reuse projection code to output us.json; in compose_lab.py, render map layer with GSAP: arc drawing (stroke-dashoffset), star pulse (scale), label fade-in, year counter (textPlugin).

title: Reproducible Asset Bake with Per-Clip Level-Set
text: Grade all stills: percentile stretch (0.6/99.6) + mild S-curve (x + 0.18*(x-0.5)*(1-|2x-1|)). Upscale clips: hqdn3d denoise → lanczos scale → unsharp. Compute one global level-set per clip (no per-frame pumping).
how: Enhance prep.py with grade() and VF filter chain; store baked assets in assets/ with manifest; use in compose.py via pre-loaded frames.

title: Deterministic Procedural Backgrounds via Seeded Noise & Instancing
text: moon.js/dusk.js generate infinite terrain, rocks (70 hero + 1000s instanced pebbles), grass blades (70), frost crystals (instanced icosahedra) using mulberry(seed) and fbm2/n2 noise. Zero asset downloads, infinite zoom, consistent across renders.
how: Replace Muse/FLUX calls for 'lab look' abstract backgrounds (grids, particle fields, terrain) with a Python/JS noise module (port mulberry/fbm2). Generate geometry/positions at render time via seeded RNG. Use for 'Kaise Tech' HUD backgrounds, data pillar grids, starfields.

title: Lossless Master → Single Encode Pipeline for Sharp Graphics
text: build.sh renders frames to PNG → FFV1 lossless MKV (master.mkv) → ONE H.264 encode (libx264, preset slow, crf 14, tune animation, High 4:2:0, BT.709). Avoids generational blur on 1-bit edges, text, and dither patterns. Audio muxed with measured loudnorm offsets.
how: Modify doctor.py/render pipeline: render HyperFrames to PNG sequence (or raw video) → FFV1 MKV → single x264 encode with -tune animation -crf 14. Drop current multi-pass or direct MP4 render. Add ffmpeg colorspace flags (bt709) for consistency.

title: Pen/Hand Shadow-Only Rendering
text: Render only soft shadows of pen/hand (not the objects) on paper. Composite hand shadow as single blurred layer (source-in tint) to avoid overlap darkening. Pen shadow is a wedge from tip scaled with zoom.
how: In drawing effects (Procedural Handwriting Physics), add shadow pass: draw pen/hand shadows to offscreen canvas, blur, composite at low opacity before main line.

title: Atkinson Error Diffusion for 1-Bit Photo Conversion
text: Use Atkinson error diffusion (not ordered dither) for photographic 1-bit prints; adjust dot pitch per output size; lift shadows before dithering. Produces organic, print-like halftones.
how: In thumb.py or image prep, add Atkinson dither option for 1-bit style thumbnails or inserts; use dot pitch matching target resolution.

title: Music Timbre Synced to Visual Complexity
text: Synthesize lead timbre as Fourier pluck: number of harmonics = current visual complexity (e.g., active circles/layers). Cold open = square wave (many harmonics); single element = pure sine; buildup = harmonics added per birth event. Bass follows chord roots. Music ducks 300 Hz–4 kHz under voice.
how: In mix.py, compute n_terms(t) from visual events (births). In fpluck(), sum sin(2π·f·h·t)/h for h=1..n_terms. Apply band-carving: music -= bp(music,300,4000)*0.5*voice_env. Balance voice 10 dB over music RMS during speech.

title: Phosphor CRT Post-Process Pass
text: Map render channels to phosphor colors: R=beam (#4DFF88), G=graticule/text (#8DFFB0), B=hot cores (#E6FFEC), A=amber overlays. Apply 4-scale Gaussian bloom (½…¹⁄₁₆, weighted), soft shoulder saturation (k=0.78), radial vignette, temporal dither (1.6/255). Optional power-off collapse (vertical→horizontal line→dot fade).
how: Add post.py step after HyperFrames render: read RGBA frames, apply Phosphor class (persist previous frame with DECAY=0), write to ffmpeg pipe. Trigger power-off at timeline 'poweroff' key. Use OpenCV for blur/resize.

title: Monotone Cubic Interpolation (Fritsch-Carlson) for Data Motion
text: lib.js exports monotone(keys) → t→value that preserves monotonicity (no overshoot) for keyframe data. Used for multi-dim tracks (track(keys)). Ideal for animating chart values, counters, progress bars without wobble.
how: Port monotone() to Python (or JS in HyperFrames). Use in compose_lab.py for stat counters, line charts, growing data pillars — any data-driven animation where overshoot looks wrong.

title: Math Formula SVG Template System
text: Pre-bake LaTeX formulas (via MathJax) into SVG path templates with digit placeholders {D0}{D1}… so any N can be rendered at runtime by swapping digit paths. formulas.json holds templates for 1/2/3-digit limits and ∞; digits 0-9 are separate paths. Zero TeX dependency at render time.
how: Add tex2svg.mjs to tools/; run once per style to generate formulas.json. In compose_lab.py, load templates, replace {D*} with digit paths for dynamic equation display (e.g., Fourier series in Kaise Tech).

title: Per-shot grading parameter reset
text: The final composite shader explicitly resets all grading parameters (exposure, vignette, saturation, contrast, lift, gain) to defaults (GRADE0) at the start of every shot, preventing color/look inheritance across segment boundaries.
how: In our render pipeline (mix.py/compose_lab.py), ensure each segment's grade settings are applied fresh by resetting to a base grade config before applying shot-specific overrides.

title: Automated subtitle darkness QC
text: A script (subcheck.py) extracts the middle frame of each subtitle cue, isolates the subtitle box region, and measures the percentage of non-text pixels darker than L=0.35; fails if any cue falls below threshold.
how: Add a step in review.py: for each rendered short, run ffmpeg to grab frames at cue midpoints, compute luminance/saturation in the subtitle safe area, and flag cues where dark background < 90%.

title: Word-level timestamps for karaoke sync
text: words.json provides per-word start/end times (relative to line start) for every narration line, enabling precise word-highlight captions, lip-sync, or SFX triggers. Generated from TTS alignment (likely Whisper).
how: After Gemini TTS, run Whisper alignment on the audio to produce word-level timestamps; store in brain.jsonl per line; use in compose_lab.py for word-light-up captions (already in lab look) and SFX event sync.

title: Shot config pattern: update/post/grade
text: Each shot module exports update(t), post(), grade() returning animation state, depth-of-field/bloom params, and color-grading params. This cleanly separates motion, optical effects, and look-dev per shot.
how: Refactor compose_lab.py shot definitions to return a dict with 'animate'(t), 'post'{focus,aper,maxCoc,bloom}, 'grade'{expo,vig,sat,contrast,lift,gain}; feed these into the render pipeline per segment.

title: Bang Emphasis Pop
text: Exclamation mark '!' scales in with strong back-ease (3.0), floats up 30px, red fill with white stroke; lasts 1.1s with fade-out.
how: Add to visual grammar for surprise moments: trigger via timeline event at key frames; render as overlay canvas in HyperFrames.

title: Typewriter Speech Bubbles with Anchor Tracking
text: Speech bubbles type at 30 CPS, anchored to speaker's head position with a curved tail; Chinese translation fades in after English completes; next-page arrow appears when done.
how: Add to hud.js equivalent in HyperFrames: create Bubble component using GSAP for typewriter, position via anchor data from layout, emit blip SFX events on even-indexed characters.

title: Action Rating Pop-ups (NICE! GREAT!)
text: Short-lived 'NICE!'/'GREAT!' words with gradient fill, ink outline, and 10 radial star-burst lines; scales in with back-ease, floats up 50px, fades out at 1.2s.
how: Implement as reusable HyperFrames component triggered by timeline events; use for quiz correct answers or milestone moments in educational shorts.

title: Deterministic character state functions
text: Each character has a pure function state(t) returning position, pose, expression, scale, etc. at time t. Enables frame-perfect sync between animation, camera, lighting, and SFX without timeline callbacks. Used for Pip, Crumple, Fold, whale, boat.
how: In HyperFrames/GSAP, adopt a similar pattern for complex sequences: write a getState(t) function per character/prop that computes all animated values. Drive GSAP tweens or direct DOM updates from this single source of truth.

title: Lighting timeline with environment crossfade
text: lightsAt(t) blends two lighting rigs: story-world (sun color/intensity for day/dusk/night) and real-world (desk lamp, hemisphere). Crossfade driven by seg(t, start, end) based on book-open and page-turn timestamps.
how: Define a lighting schedule in story.js (or plan.py output) with phases (intro, act1, act2...). In compose_lab.py, interpolate light colors/intensities per phase. Use for panel shine, HUD glow, background gradients.

title: Beat-matched music jump editing
text: Use librosa to analyze music beats, chroma, and timbre; find two beat-similar segments (8+ beats apart, same downbeat phase) that allow a seamless jump cut to hit a target duration. Implemented in jump.py/jump2.py with self-similarity matrices.
how: Add a music_edit.py step after script lock: analyze chosen track, compute jump points for exact video duration, output edit points for mix.py. Uses free librosa/NumPy.

title: Procedural Jointed Character Rig with FK and Expression Swaps
text: girl.js defines a paper-cut figure (head, torso, upper/fore arms, thighs, shins, scissors) as cached Canvas pieces. Forward kinematics from pelvis root places each limb via rotation matrices. Five swappable face expressions (smile, surprise, scared, determined, sleep) and three hand states (open, fist, flat). Scissors are a separate two-blade prop attached to hand.
how: Build a `PaperCharacter` class in our visual stack: define joint hierarchy (pelvis → hip/knee/ankle, neck/shoulder/elbow/wrist), cache piece canvases at startup, expose `draw(pose)` where pose is a dict of joint angles + expression + hand state. Use for recurring characters in Puraan Ki Katha (e.g., Hanuman, Krishna).

title: Procedural Folk Motif Library
text: A set of pure JS functions (sawRow, crescentRows, swirl, doubleSwirl, plum, rosette, coin, strands) that generate authentic Chinese paper-cut patterns (sawtooth, crescent scales, cloud curls, plum blossoms, coin holes, hair strands) as cut-out paths. All are deterministic, parameterized, and composable.
how: Port motifs.js to TypeScript for HyperFrames; use in Puraan Ki Katha for mythological borders, transitions, and decorative elements. Call from compose_lab.py or new motif components.

title: Deterministic Seeded Noise Utility
text: paper.js provides h2(x,y,s) hash, tileNoise(period) for value noise, and rnd(k,s) for 1D sequences. All visual jitter (paper fibers, cut edges, wob, snowflakes) uses these with fixed seeds per piece, ensuring frame-exact reproducibility across renders.
how: Extract a noise.ts module with the same APIs. Replace ad-hoc Math.random() in HyperFrames components (grain, jitter, particle systems) with seeded calls keyed by piece ID and frame number.

title: Backlit Transmission Shader for Paper-Cut Look
text: paper.js implements transmitOf(piece) that creates a transmission texture: paper color multiplied by fiber noise (overlay), then masked by piece alpha. Holes become transparent. Drawn with globalCompositeOperation='multiply' over a light field for authentic backlit paper glow.
how: Add a HyperFrames filter component (TransmissionPass) that takes a layer, generates a transmission texture via offscreen canvas (using our paperGrain), and composites with multiply. Use for Puraan Ki Katha 'paper manuscript' scenes and Kaise Tech 'lab notes' aesthetic.

title: Deterministic kinematics with trapezoidal velocity profiles
text: plot.js models every pen move (pen-up: VU=260mm/s, AU=2600mm/s²; pen-down: VD=90mm/s, AD=1300mm/s²), Z-axis (T_Z=0.32s), gripper (T_GRIP=0.16s), drop/lift (T_DROP=0.085s, T_LIFT=0.07s). Time for distance L: if L ≥ v²/a → L/v + v/a else 2√(L/a). Position at τ: quadratic accel, linear cruise, quadratic decel. plotState(P) returns exact {x,y,z,held,grip,n,cur,v,down} for any machine time P.
how: Adopt for our 'procedural UI/prop factory' and 'mechanical arm' animations in compose_lab.py. Define kinematic params per prop type (slider, dial, plotter, 3D printer). Use in preflight.py to compute exact motion durations → sync voice pace. Replace GSAP easing with physics-based timing for 'lab look' credibility.

title: End card as animated pen-stroke reveal
text: drawEnd(t) renders 5 end-card lines (title, EN, CN, style, sign) stroke-by-stroke in paper-colored ink (#e8473a for title, #efe7d6 for rest). Each line has start time ENDT[i] and duration (0.4s first, 0.24s rest). Budget = revealed_fraction × total_stroke_length; draws full strokes until budget exhausted, then partial final stroke. Subtle grain lines (56×7px) fade in at t=46.9s.
how: In thumb.py / compose_lab.py end-card component: store title strokes as SVG paths with lengths. Animate stroke-dashoffset from total → 0 per line with staggered starts. Use paper-colored stroke (theme-dependent). Add 1px grain lines as CSS keyframes. Replaces static thumbnail frame with 2s animated loop for Instagram Reels cover.

title: Multi-resolution paper texture with bump mapping
text: main.js creates a base 6144px whole-sheet texture (6144/SHW px/mm) plus 5 shot-specific patches (e.g., shot 4: 140×138mm at 22px/mm, shot 6: 258×92mm at 20px/mm). Each patch re-renders only strokes intersecting its window. Bump map from 512² procedural grain tile (repeated). Patches swapped at shot boundaries via visibility toggle.
how: In compose.py/compose_lab.py, replace single Ken Burns photo with a texture atlas: generate base at 4K, render patches at 8K for close-up shots. Use CanvasTexture with mipmaps. Switch via shot ID in render loop. Reduces VRAM vs full 8K sheet; keeps crisp text on close-ups.

title: Procedural pictogram library (parametric SVG/Canvas components)
text: A small set of parametric drawing functions (umbrella, raindrop, cloud, sun, moon, bolt, footprint, lost items) drawn with code, not assets. Each takes (ctx, x, y, scale, state, colors) and renders consistently at any resolution. Enables infinite variations without asset management.
how: Port the pictogram drawing functions (engine.js) into a HyperFrames component library (e.g., components/pictograms/*.js) that emit SVG or Canvas 2D paths. Use them in compose_lab.py for recurring icons (tech logos, myth symbols, UI markers) with themeable colors from the palette.

title: Deterministic procedural background patterns with row offsets
text: A grid of 180px cells, each filled with a seeded motif (discs, waves, pictograms). Whole-row horizontal offsets (per-row function of time) create infinite scrolling parallax. Pattern is baked to an offscreen canvas once per seed, then drawn with drawImage per row. Seed + spread + density + palette = reproducible look.
how: Implement a PatternGenerator class in HyperFrames (JS module) that creates a large offscreen canvas from a seed, motif set, and palette. In compose_lab.py, call it for lab-look backgrounds (HUD panels, terminal scenes) and animate row offsets via GSAP on a beat grid. Cache baked patterns per shot config.

title: Expression Transition via Blink Interpolation
text: Never hard-cut facial expressions. Transition through a blink: scale eye Y to 0.06 (6% open) over 2–3 frames, swap expression, scale back. Controlled by faceK (1=open, 0=closed) passed to expression renderer. Eliminates uncanny pops.
how: Apply to Procedural Jointed Character Rig (brain item). In character expression swap logic, insert blink keyframe (faceK=0.06) at midpoint. Use existing 'RPG Dialog Box Grammar' timing for blink duration.

title: Perspective-Corrected End Card via Raycast
text: End card is a decal on the 3D board. Raycast the final frame's screen rectangle (e.g., 1180–1800 px, 812–1036 px) onto board plane to get world coords. Pre-stretch vertical by 1/perspective_squash so text reads undistorted from camera.
how: For lab-look shorts with 3D board/floor (Kaise Tech), implement in compose_lab.py end-card component: compute board-plane UV rect from camera, draw card to offscreen canvas with vertical scale compensation, apply as texture.

title: Color-depth-matched audio fidelity tiers
text: Match Foley/music bit-depth and sample-rate to visual style: 4-color sections use 4-bit/11kHz crushed audio; 8-bit sections use 8-bit/22kHz mono; 16-bit sections use full 48kHz stereo with SNES-style echo. Ensures cohesive AV texture.
how: In mix.py, add a 'fidelity' tag per scene (lab/classic/story) and apply crush/resample/echo per tag. Use existing loudness mastering after.

title: Shader-based crisp grid/diagram layer
text: WebGL shader draws resolution-independent grid lines, paper grain, and edge ink on a board mesh. Stays sharp at any camera distance/zoom — ideal for data diagrams during Ken Burns moves.
how: Add a Three.js render pass in HyperFrames for 'diagram' scenes. Port stage.js board shader (gridL, hsh grain) to a custom GSAP-compatible WebGL layer.

title: Bayer dithering transition library
text: Use Bayer matrix (1/2/4-bit) for dissolve, wipe, and mosaic transitions. Provides retro, crisp, deterministic transitions that sync to beat grid via threshold animation.
how: Implement bayer8(x,y) in px.js port. Add transition components in compose_lab.py: BayerDissolve, BayerWipe, MosaicSweep. Drive threshold by beat events.

title: Torch flame animation via 4-frame shape arrays at 12 fps
text: Flame shapes defined as arrays of widths per height (shape[frame][i]). Lean alternates per frame. Colors: white core → yellow → amber → orange → rust edges. Glow is a separate Bayer-dithered radial pass.
how: For fire/energy effects in lab look, define 4-frame SVG path arrays. Animate with GSAP timeline at 12 fps (frameDuration: 1/12). Add radial glow via filter with Bayer noise texture.

title: Dialogue box component with typing effect and color-depth skins
text: dialog() renders a window with three skins (SNES blue-gradient, NES mono, GB 4-color), optional portrait, per-character typing at 38 cps, cursor blink, and automatic word-wrap. Skins swap entire palette via LUT.
how: Build a HyperFrames DialogueBox component: props for skin (palette), portrait, text, cps. Use GSAP to reveal characters. Skin prop swaps a CSS filter or SVG <feComponentTransfer> LUT. Reuse for RPG-style explainers.

title: Procedural prop generators with frame caching
text: crystal() pre-renders 8 rotation frames (90° symmetry) into a Map cache. door() generates full geometry (voussoirs, keystone, leaves, rune ring) procedurally per frame. pedestal() uses ASCII map. All deterministic, no external assets.
how: Create a props/ module in HyperFrames: write generators for recurring icons (save crystal, terminal, HUD elements) that output SVG/Canvas frames and cache them. Use for consistent end-cards and UI elements.

title: Deterministic Hash-Based Tile Variation
text: A grid of tiles (600 px cells) each shows a banana variant. Variant, rotation, flip, and misalignment are derived from hash(i, j, seed) so the wall is identical every render. Clones flip to unique variants on a timed wave (flipT = base + dist * 0.13 + hash * 0.09).
how: In ideas.py/research.py, when scripting 'many kinds' (mythology avatars, tech models), generate a tile grid with seeded hash for pose/color/label. Use in compose_lab.py's panel grid; flip timing driven by timeline events.

title: Giant Mosaic Composition from Tile Edges
text: The same tile wall forms a giant banana silhouette. A precomputed list of cell edges (G_EDGES) between inside/outside cells is sorted by angle from the tip; the black key line draws along these edges progressively (eio easing), locking exactly to the mosaic grid.
how: For 'many → one' stories (e.g., 1000 banana kinds → single export banana), build a tile atlas, compute inside/outside via a signed-distance field, extract edges, and animate a strokeVar line along them in compose_lab.py.

title: Rot-Spread Visualization (Propagating Dots)
text: A red/blue dot front (fr) sweeps left-to-right across the tile wall; tiles ahead of the front get overprinted with increasing red+blue density (d = clamp((fr - x)/2400) * 0.9). Behind the front, tiles are fully darkened. Metaphor for disease/idea spread.
how: In script plan, add a 'spread_front' event with position over time; in compose_lab.py, apply a plate overprint to panels whose x < front. Reuses existing plate over() logic.

title: Hard cut + match cut camera choreography from keyframe arrays
text: Three camera segments (CAMS[0..2]) each an array of keyframes {t, el, az, d, x, y, z, ox, oy}. Hermite interpolation between keys. Hard cut at 18.9s (dial → top-down plate). Match cut at 33.0s (plate → escapement close-up) with identical view parameters.
how: Define camera moves in plan.py as keyframe arrays with spherical coords + viewOffset. Add a 'cut' type in timeline.js that switches active keyframe set. Implement hermite interpolation in compose_lab.py for smooth Ken Burns / 3D-like moves.

title: Color-coded system dye propagation
text: Each subsystem (power/transmission/regulator) receives its hue from a 3D origin point; a radial shader spread (radius R * easeOut) colors parts over 0.4–0.7 s. Implemented in film.js via DYE array and per-group uniforms (O, R).
how: Add a 'dye' pass to HyperFrames: assign each visual element a system tag and origin (x,y). In compose_lab.py, animate a CSS/Canvas radial gradient mask per tag using the same easeOut curve. Trigger from timeline cues.

title: Soft cel shader with per-part colored outlines
text: Outlines are a darker shade of the part's own system color (mix(col*0.52, ink, 0.28)), not black. Two-pass render: color (MSAA) + normals/depth; composite detects depth steps and normal creases. Outline.js fragment shader uses 4-direction Laplacian + normal delta.
how: Port to HyperFrames via a post-render Canvas filter: render scene to offscreen, run Sobel on depth+normal buffers (can approximate with SVG filter feMorphology + feColorMatrix), tint edges per element's system color. Add to compose_lab.py as optional 'cel' style.

title: Procedural tick/foley synthesis from parametric metal clicks
text: mix.py tick() builds a beat from three decaying sinusoids (3.15/4.87/6.92 kHz) + filtered noise, with tick/tock pitch alternation (0.93×). bigtick adds a 70 Hz thump. metal_swish() and clack() use bandpassed noise + resonant tails. Zero samples, fully deterministic (seeded RNG).
how: Replace SFX library in mix.py with these generators. Add tick(t, bright), swish(d, f0, f1), clack(v, f) functions. Use for any mechanical/horology short. Seed RNG per project for reproducibility.

title: Deterministic procedural gear geometry (involute + club-tooth)
text: gears.js generates involute spur profiles (module, teeth, pressure angle, backlash) and Swiss club-tooth escape wheels. Spoke windows via convex hull of circles + Chaikin smoothing. Mainspring/hairspring as spiral strips with r(θ) functions. All pure math, no assets.
how: Build a 'mech-kit' module for HyperFrames: export SVG paths for gears, pinions, escape wheels, springs at any scale. Use in compose_lab.py for 'how it works' shorts. Parameterize by tooth count, module, spoke count. Cache as JSON.

title: Bilingual subtitle timing driven by primary language
text: Chinese narration sets the pace: voice/zh/dur.json (generated by TTS) defines each line's display window. English subtitles use the same windows (shifted -0.05s start, +0.45s end, clamped to next line). Per-line rate overrides in JSON (+25% for dense facts) keep both languages in sync without manual timing.
how: In plan.py, write lines_hi.json and lines_en.json with 'rate' field per line. TTS step generates dur.json for Hindi (primary). Subtitle generator reads dur.json, applies same windows to English with small lead/lag. Eliminates manual subtitle timing.

title: Tiered Build Dependency Check
text: Build script (build.sh) verifies heavy dependency tiers before starting: checks `numba` for music synthesis, then runs fonts → TTS → ASR → score → events → mix → subs → render → mux. Fails fast with clear instruction if tier missing.
how: In `build.sh` (or `doctor.py` preflight), add tier checks: `python -c 'import numba'` for audio synthesis, `python -c 'import fontTools'` for subsetting, `node -e 'require("canvas")'` for headless render. Print `Run: sh setup.sh deps voice music` on failure. Integrate with `doctor.py` 10-min self-repair.

title: Overprint Simulation for Print Aesthetic
text: Simulate risograph overprint by drawing layers with `globalCompositeOperation='lighter'` (additive) on offscreen canvas, then stamping with knockout halo. In draw.js, `over(fn)` sets `lighter`; `layer(fn, halo)` draws on transparent layer, adds 5px white outline via rotated copies, then composites. Produces color mixing (blue+yellow=green) where shapes overlap.
how: In HyperFrames `compose_lab.py`, add `overprint` render mode: create offscreen canvas, draw base plates with `lighter`, apply halo knockout, then composite to main canvas. Use for 'lab look' print-style overlays (stat counters, UI panels). Seed ensures deterministic overlap.

title: Plate-based color system for consistent branding
text: Define palette as 3-component vectors (blue, yellow, pink density). Each asset (character, UI panel, prop) specifies color per plate. Adding a plate adds a color (blue → blue+yellow=green → blue+yellow+pink=full). Enables "plates = story" progression: each location/act introduces a new plate.
how: Design system for lab look: base 3 spot colors (e.g., tech blue, warning yellow, accent pink). In compose_lab.py, UI components declare plate mask [1,0,0], [1,1,0], etc. Riso shader or direct compositing applies.

title: Watercolor Wash Recipe
text: `wash(pts, col)`: 1) Flat fill. 2) Blurred elliptical noise mottling (110 max, rgba 30/255 @ 3-8% opacity). 3) Edge pooling: blurred stroke (7px, 26px wide, rgba 20 @ 16%). 4) Thin outline (3.2px, #2A2927). Cached to large canvas.
how: Document in `style_guide.md` for AI prompt engineering (Muse/FLUX): 'watercolor wash, mid-grey paper, soft mottling, pigment pooling edges, thin charcoal outline, no boiling'.

title: Material Foley Synthesis Library
text: `mix.py` `RECIPES` dict maps event types to parametric synthesis: porcelain (high inharmonic partials), ceramic_low, woodblock, sugar_crunch (HP noise), rubber_creak (FM saw), water_splash (LP noise + sweeps), china_crash (porcelain volley). All seeded, deterministic.
how: Port `RECIPES` to `core/audio/sfx.py`; replace static SFX cues in `mix.py` with event-type calls; drive from `events.json` `type` field.

title: Optical Film Mastering Pass (Audio+Visual)
text: Audio: `optical()` bandwidth 110-6200Hz, wow/flutter (0.6Hz+7Hz), tanh saturation, crackle/hiss/projector noise. Visual: `film.js` gate weave, flicker, scratches, dust, hairs, vignette, rounded gate. Both keyed to frame count.
how: Add `optical_master.py` (audio) and `film_post.js` (HyperFrames overlay) as optional `--style=film` flag in `render.py`; reuse `vnoise`/`hash` from `/core/lib.js`.

title: Music cue sheet tied to bar/beat grid with instrumentation notes
text: CUES array: each cue has bars [start,end], key, and detailed note (e.g., 'xylophone eighths rising C D E F G A B from 11.2; tuba quarters from 12.2'). Drives procedural score and hit points.
how: Adopt in ideas.py/research.py: when planning music bed, write cue sheet in bars/beats; feed to procedural music synth (future) or human composer for precise hit alignment.

title: Iris transition with diegetic hand interaction
text: Iris closes on mug; a hand reaches from inside the circle, grabs the edge, and pulls it shut (shotIris). Signature transition reused across sections.
how: Design as a reusable transition component in HyperFrames; trigger on chapter end. Adds 'Identical transition signature across sections' with character.

title: Beat-synced animation primitives (walk/run/hop/breath)
text: Reusable functions `walk(p)`, `run(p)`, `hop(u,h)`, `breath(t)` locked to 144 BPM grid; characters animate on twos (12fps), camera continuous. All motion derives from `beats(t)` and `q(t)` (frame-quantized time).
how: Add to compose_lab.py as `motion_primitives.py`; use in scene plans for any character/prop to auto-breathe, walk, or react on beat without keyframes.

title: Noodle limb system (quadratic curve with taper & bend)
text: `noodle(a,b,bend,w0,w1)` returns a tapered, round-capped limb as a closed path; used for arms/legs/hoses. Bend is perpendicular offset; width interpolates.
how: Add to chars.js equivalent; enables rubber-hose character rigging for mascots or explainer avatars without skeletal animation.

title: HUD Overlay: Altitude, Scale Bar, Lock Brackets
text: Persistent analyst HUD shows altitude (km), a dynamic scale bar (km, round numbers 1/2/5/10…), and animated search/lock brackets on the target. Reinforces "satellite briefing" credibility and provides spatial context.
how: Add `HUD` component to `compose_lab.py`: reads camera `alt`, `F`, `tgt` each frame; draws altitude top-right, scale bar bottom-right (max 240 px), brackets on projected target. Style: mono font, thin hairlines, halo.

title: Distance-field map layer for resolution-independent coastlines
text: Generate an RGB plate: R = distance inside shore (0–60 km), G = distance outside shore (0–60 km), B = relief luminance. Shader uses R/G for crisp coast at any zoom, B for hill-shade. Built from vector polygons (Natural Earth) rasterized at plate resolution.
how: Adopt in compose_lab.py for animated map scenes. Use tools/mapfield.py logic: rasterize historic sea polygon, compute EDT with km sampling, sample Blue Marble for relief. Store as mapfield.png + plates.json metadata.

title: Growth animation via normalized distance transform
text: For 'water returning' or 'spread' effects: compute Euclidean distance transform from old boundary mask to new area pixels. Normalize 97th percentile to 1, clamp 0.004–1, Gaussian blur 1px. Use as shader mask for progressive reveal on beat.
how: Implement in growth.py style for any before/after mask pair (e.g., flood, deforestation, urban sprawl). Feed to lab look shader as 'growth' texture. Already have Rot-Spread Visualization in brain; this gives the math.

title: Audio-visual onset alignment gate
text: Compute spectral-flux onsets on the final mix (hop 512, win 1024). Every timeline key event (lock, map_on, touch, ring, stop, label, range_end, whip, dam, nring, pin, end) must have an onset within ±60 ms. Report count and list outliers.
how: Extend review.py after render: run onset detection (numpy/scipy) on mix.wav, load timeline.json T keys, compare. Log failures; optionally fail if >0. Adapted from tools/audiocheck.py.

title: Deterministic asset fetch with manifest logging
text: Every external asset request (images, tiles, data) logs URL, plate/asset name, and access date to assets/raw/manifest.jsonl (JSON Lines). Enables reproducibility, provenance, and cache invalidation.
how: Wrap all fetch calls (Muse, FLUX, Pollinations, Wikimedia, map tiles) in a logger that appends to manifest.jsonl. Follows tools/fetch_gibs.py and fetch_landsat.py pattern. Integrates with existing Automated Asset Provenance Tracker.

title: Universe Tags as Typed Terminal Readout
text: TAGS in story.js define [start, end, code, description, bg, fg]; main.js tag() types them char-by-char in a VT323 retro terminal box with pop-in scale. Great for Kaise Tech lab section headers.
how: In compose_lab.py, add a TagComponent that reads tag data from timeline, renders a fixed-position terminal box, types text at 40-110 chars/sec with blinking cursor, uses brand colors per section.

title: Subtitle Speaker Blocks with Boil & Pop-In
text: Subtitles render as speaker-colored rounded blocks (VASK teal, GARY orange, COFFEE brown) with 11px boiling outline, back-ease pop-in, auto-wrap at 1300px, max two lines on screen.
how: Extend thumb.py/subtitle burner: add speaker color map, boiling outline via SVG filter or canvas, pop-in animation using GSAP back.easeOut, word-wrap logic at 1300px, limit to two active lines.

title: Contact Sheet & Frame Strip Generation
text: sheet.sh and strip.sh render frames at intervals, tile them into a single JPEG via ffmpeg for quick visual QA. Used before final render to catch timing/artifacts.
how: Add a preflight contact-sheet step: render every N seconds (e.g., 0.5s) via headless browser, montage with ImageMagick/ffmpeg, save to dashboard. Trigger manually or on failed review.py.

title: Per-Character Voice Post-Processing
text: voice.py applies character-specific EQ (VASK: saturation + low-mid boost; GARY: high-mid lift), pitch shift (COFFEE +7 semitones), and truncation with fade. Ensures distinct voices from same TTS engine.
how: Insert a voice_post.py after tts.py: load lines.json, apply per-speaker EQ curves (peaking biquads), optional pitch_shift, normalize to -0.95 peak. Write processed wavs to voices/ and update dur.json.

title: World vs Screen Space Particle Layers (Marine Snow Parallax)
text: specks(cam, seed, n, x0,x1,y0,y1, {fall, t}) projects world metres → screen, falls with time. screenSnow(seed, n, vx, vy, t, {streak}) draws in screen px with parallax velocity. Both use seeded RNG. World snow respects camera zoom; screen snow gives cheap depth layers.
how: In compose_lab.py particle system: split emitters into 'world' (attached to 3D camera via prl) and 'screen' (fixed viewport, velocity parallax). Use for dust, UI glitches, data sparklines. Reduces overdraw when camera pushes in.

title: Deterministic Procedural Organic Prop Factory
text: crab.js: carapace via superellipse (n=3.4) with parametric teeth; legs as hierarchical capsule segments (taper/flat); claws with mitten hair (950 instanced cylinders); rope as twisted dual-strand tubes on Catmull-Rom curve (220 segments, Frenet frames). All seeded (mulberry) for frame-exact reproducibility. Exports ghost leg for motion-artifact pass.
how: Port math to HyperFrames Canvas 2D/GSAP or Three.js in lab look; add ProceduralPropFactory class with makeCrab(seed), makeRope(path,seed). Use for 'creature close-up' beats in Puraan Ki Katha / Kaise Tech.

title: Dual-view scan curtain transition
text: Top and side X-ray views share a moving vertical curtain (split=0.8) that sweeps left-to-right during scanning. The curtain markers appear on both views simultaneously, reinforcing the 'scanning' metaphor diegetically.
how: In compose_lab.py, add a shared `scanProgress` uniform to dual-panel layouts; drive a clip-path line across both panels synced to voice 'scanning' beats.

title: CT reconstruction with progressive noise settling
text: The CT shot renders a 3D volume with `noise = 0.5 * (1 - progress)^1.5`; noise starts high and clears over 0.55 s while the camera orbits. A 'MOTION DETECTED' HUD flag blinks when the leg moves.
how: For data-reveal scenes (maps, charts, 3D models), add a `reconstructionNoise` uniform that decays on a cubic curve; show a diegetic 'PROCESSING' badge while noise > 0.1.

title: Procedural props at real-world scale with X-ray materials
text: Every prop (suitcase, laptop, bottle, crabs) is built in metres using `boxShell`, `cylShell`, `lathe`, `tube` with material constants (ORG, MET, CELL, PCB) that map to X-ray colours. Dimensions match real objects (e.g., 20000 mAh power bank = 144×27×72 mm).
how: When designing lab-look props in compose_lab.py, author a `props.js`-style library with real measurements and material tags; use the same scale bars and dimension lines from `measurement-based visual grammar` for on-screen callouts.

title: Bilingual on-screen label helper (bi function)
text: A reusable `bi(cn, en, x, y, size_cn, size_en, color_cn, color_en)` draws Chinese above English, registers the bounding box for read-check (TX array), and returns width for alignment. Used for every UI verdict, measurement, and summary row.
how: Port `bi` into compose_lab.py as a HyperFrames component; use it for all on-screen bilingual plates (stat counters, rules, end cards) so read-check gates catch overflow automatically.

title: Verdict stamp with pop-in and bilingual text
text: `stamp(x, y, ok, k, cn, en)` draws a check/cross that scales from 1.25→1 with elastic ease, fills a rounded panel, and writes Chinese/English verdict lines. Registered for read-check when `k>0.5`.
how: Create a `VerdictStamp` GSAP component in compose_lab.py; trigger on scene verdict events (banned/allowed, fact-check pass/fail) with the same elastic pop and read-check registration.

title: Thickness-Accumulation X-Ray Compositing
text: Render meshes double-sided additive (back faces +distance, front faces −distance) × density into three material-class channels (R organic, G inorganic, B metal). A colouriser shader converts path-length sums to dual-energy hues. No depth test, pure additive blending.
how: Adapt for lab-look cutaway diagrams: draw SVG paths twice (front/back) with additive blending into an offscreen canvas, accumulate per-material thickness, then map to colour via a lookup. Use in compose_lab.py for tech internals (phones, batteries).

title: Silhouette Compositing with Directional Rim Light
text: Draw shape to mask (white). 1) Fill mask with dark colour (source-in). 2) Blur mask, offset opposite light direction, destination-out to cut rim. 3) Fill rim with warm colour (source-in). 4) Composite dark + rim with globalAlpha. Single canvas, no WebGL.
how: Implement in compose_lab.py for puppet/hand silhouettes. Use Canvas2D globalCompositeOperation ('source-in', 'destination-out') in a pre-render step. Light direction from scene key light.

title: Feather/Plume Physics with Rest Curvature
text: Chain of segments with rest angle per joint (k) + dynamic deflection array. Tapered ribbon geometry built from perpendiculars. Cross-bars alternate colour. Deterministic, pre-simulated at 120 Hz into Float32Array.
how: Add to motion library for lingzi, hair, ribbons, cable runs. Pre-simulate in a worker, store as JSON, drive via GSAP timeline. Parameterize rest curvature, stiffness, length.

title: Subtitle Plaque with Seal Component
text: Black-lacquered rounded rect (wood grain gradient), thin gold inner stroke, vermilion square seal with centred Chinese character '说' (Ma Shan Zheng font). Text in Cormorant Garamond 600. Slide-in from bottom, fade per line.
how: Build as HyperFrames component (hud_plaque.ts) for Puraan Ki Katha. Parameterize seal character, plaque colour, font. Use in thumb.py for series-branded thumbnails.

title: Microtonal Mode for Myth/Folk
text: Kuyin (bitter) mode: tonic D, fa↑ +5.4 semitones, si↓ +10.5 semitones (microtonal). Huanyin (joyful) pentatonic: D E F# A B. Banhu slides target these offsets. Gives authentic Chinese opera feel; applicable to Indian ragas with shruti offsets.
how: In music/score.py (or new raga.py), define SHRUTI = {'komal_re': 1.5, 'komal_ga': 3.5, ...} offsets in semitones. Modify banhu_note slide targets to use SHRUTI. Use for Puraan Ki Katha background score.

title: Theater Frame with Light Spill
text: Wooden frame drawn in screen space: lintel (cloud scrolls + gold fret), posts (gradient), stage lip. Inner edges receive warm spill via multiply→lighter composite: linear gradient rgba(255,170,90,0.32*spill)→0. Audience silhouettes bob at 1.3Hz. Creates diegetic 'screen' context for shadow-puppet style.
how: In compose_lab.py, add draw_frame(g, cam, spill) ported from stage.js. Call before HUD layer. Spill intensity driven by scene 'lamp_count' from timeline. Use for Puraan Ki Katha 'shadow play' episodes.

title: Procedural Damage Progression
text: Ground cracks grow with burn parameter (0–1): each crack has random seed 'd'; visible when burn*1.3 > d; length = pts * min(1, (burn*1.3 - d)*2.2); width = 1.5 + 7*progress. Cached at 24 steps (key = round(burn*24)).
how: Add core/visual/damage.py with CrackSystem(seed, num_cracks). Method get_piece(burn) returns cached canvas piece. Use in compose_lab.py for 'scorched earth', 'cracking statue', 'drying lake' scenes.

title: Automated Model Sheet Generation
text: Single render pass produces 5-panel QA sheet: (A) assembled character on lit screen with rods, (B) exploded 11 hide pieces with joint markers, (C) all 10 sun variants + crow fall states, (D) 4 key poses with rod positions, (E) head close-up, dye swatches, 10-step light ramp. Output at 1920x1080.
how: Add --q scene=modelSheet to core/render/still.mjs. Implement modelSheet() in test.js port. Run via doctor.py after style changes. Save to runs/<date>/model_sheet.jpg for Telegram approval.

title: Deterministic Pitch Glide (Warp)
text: warp(x, semis_fn) does variable-speed resampling: output length adapts to pitch curve semis(t). Used for gong pitch drop (kuang), banhu slides, suona glides. Phase accumulator: r = 2**(semis/12), ph = cumsum(r), linear interp. Sample-accurate, no phase vocoder.
how: Add warp() to core/audio/sfx.py. Replace manual pitch automation in mix.py (gong drop, arrow whoosh) with warp(sound, lambda t: drop * clip(t/0.4,0,1)**0.7). Enables expressive Foley with code.

title: 3D-to-2D Head Feature Mapping
text: Draws facial features (eyes, brows, nose, mouth) by projecting 3D local points onto a 2D plane based on head yaw. Features like the nose protrusion are handled by calculating the silhouette extreme at specific height rows.
how: Use the `headOutline` and `face` logic in `heads.js` to create dynamic avatars for 'Kaise Tech'. This allows the AI to change the 'look' direction of an explainer character via a single 'yaw' value.

title: XDoG Edge & Wash Pipeline
text: A WebGL2 pipeline using Extended Difference of Gaussians (XDoG) to extract ink-like edges from images. It combines this with luminance posterization (wash steps) and procedural hatching to turn any photo or video into a hand-drawn sketch.
how: Add to `compose_lab.py` as a post-process shader. Pass Muse-generated images through this `Redraw` filter to create a consistent 'hand-inked' look for tech explainers or mythology stories.

title: Prop Attachment via Rig Solver (palmsAt)
text: Compute prop attachment points (e.g., loaf between hands) from the solved rig joint positions (wrist + hand) at render time, not hardcoded offsets. Handles yaw, scale, and pose changes without popping.
how: In HyperFrames character components, expose `getPalmCenter(side)` from the pose solver. Update prop components (held objects, speech bubbles) to read this coordinate each frame. Remove manual `x/y` offsets for held items.

title: Film Look Pass: Ink/Hatch Parameters
text: The Redraw pass uses bilateral filter (sigma=1.3, p=24) -> hatch thresholds (h1=0.55, h2=0.72, h3=0.88) -> gap=5 -> gamma=0.9. These specific values create the 'etched plate' look. Adopt for `compose_lab.py` post-process.
how: In `compose_lab.py` final pass (or new `film_post.py`), apply OpenCV bilateralFilter + custom hatch shader (or PIL) with these exact params. Add `film_look: 'silent_etch'` preset. Test on Kaise Tech 'lab' thumbnails.

title: Rhythmic tension/release as narrative hook
text: Structure the first 15–20s around a clear rhythmic conflict: the ensemble locks to a grid, one character is consistently off-grid (half-beat late). The audience feels the tension. At the midpoint, a 'count-in' forces the off-grid character onto the beat — the release becomes the climax. Works for any process where one element lags then syncs (learning, debugging, team sync).
how: In ideas.py, add a 'rhythmic_conflict' template: identify a repeating beat in the topic (release cycle, sprint, heartbeat, clock). Assign protagonist as the late one. Plan the count-in moment at ~60% duration. In plan.py, enforce a musical grid (120 BPM = 0.5s beat) and schedule the late hits at beat+0.25s until the count-in.

title: Runway rings as persistent visual memory
text: Each footfall leaves a growing ring on the water that decays over 40s. Later shots show the full trail of rings receding to the horizon, visually encoding the entire history of the run. The rings survive music cuts and silence, becoming a diegetic timeline the audience reads subconsciously.
how: In plan.py, for any repetitive action (steps, heartbeats, code commits, deployments), add a 'persistent_trail' visual: a ring/bar/dot that spawns on each event, grows to a max size, then fades with a long tail (two exponentials: fast 1.6s, slow 40s). In compose_lab.py, render trails in a separate layer that persists across shots. Use the same event times that drive audio.

title: Split-fountain gradient pulls
text: A single squeegee pull can carry multiple ink beads (segments along x) each with its own color (scenes.js fountain array). The engine renders each bead through a vertical clip strip, producing smooth multi-color gradients in one pass — perfect for sky gradients or multi-hue titles.
how: In plan.py, allow a 'fountain' property on background pulls listing color stops. In compose_lab.py, implement a split-fountain renderer that draws each color segment through a moving vertical clip (wipeRegion) during the pull.

title: Persistent data prop (ticket stub)
text: A ticket stub (DAY, FROM HOME km, LANDMARK, BUILT year) stays fixed on screen across cities. Its fields animate in with wipeRegion pulls; numbers update live during the return journey (count-up). It acts as a diegetic data dashboard.
how: In plan.py, define a 'stub' component with fields and pull timings. In compose_lab.py, render it in screen space (fixed coordinates) using wipeRegion for each field. Reuse the 'Diegetic Prop Tray' brain entry for persistence across shots.

title: Squeegee/pull transition between scenes
text: A re-ink sweep (sweep()) reveals the next city: a tilted squeegee blade with ink beads (split-fountain colors) wipes across the screen. The blade position comes from swFront (leading edge of wipeRegion). Beads roll and stretch realistically.
how: Create a transition component in compose_lab.js that takes two scene draw functions, a progress p, angle, and bead colors. Draw scene A, clip scene B with swRegion(p), draw squeegee at swFront(p). Use for section transitions (Beijing→Istanbul, etc.).
